10.title: For Parents--It's Rated PG-13 for a Reason
10.content:
For parents who are looking for a thought provoking movie where you're getting you money's worth, DON'T bring pre-teens.

The movie is very well acted by all, especially notable was Joseph Gordon-Levitt's performance who, at one of the most critical points in the movie, is able to think clearly, improvise, and is the only one aware (as far as I could make out of it) that his actions/inactions will save the day for the mission and his comrades.

With that caveat, let me say that this is a movie that I found thoroughly captivating, and at nearly 2 1/2 hours long, could have had some careful editing to shorten the length of a few scenes but very few.

I could have missed it, but didn't notice any Eff-bombs, and the violence is reserved for the dream sequences (which make up probably 95% of the flick) and like most dreams there are elements (even violent) that don't seem to make any sense even for pacifists or ones who consider themselves very moral.

On the morality point, there are many lessons here for all, and it is clearly evident to those in the film, from trust to regret to redemption.

Unless your child is very intelligent, leave them at home and promise to take them to "Despicable Me" or something else they'll understand.

If you choose to forgo the above, do yourself and the audience in the theater a favor--bring duct tape, and be prepared to use it.

If you don't, after the first dozen "What's happening," "Is it real," "I don't understand," etc, your theater neighbors will no doubt be more than willing to escort the kids, and you, to the nearest exit.

This is a complex, thinking person's movie. It's not a DVD that you can pause and take however long (if even possible) to try to help your kids to understand.

That doesn't mean that the totality of the movie is impossible to understand for an adult, and there is just enough, left to your own imagination, that you can interpret parts, the ending, or the entire movie in alternate ways.

This is not to infer that you'll be throwing your money away going to see the movie--far from it, it's the type of thought provoking movie that will have you re-running in your own mind, and/or discussing it with others for some time.

But save yourself some money if you have the kind of wonderful, loving, normal pre-teens that most of us do--and this isn't a challenge for those who are convinced that their kids are the exceptional few who will understand what's going on without having to play 20,000 questions during the first 15 minutes.

You've been warned, and your fellow theater-goers WILL be bringing their own duct tape for the ?-askers.

10.title: Very creative idea with epic plot
10.content:
From my point of view, Inception is the film that lies at the second place of Nolan's films.

Like Interstellar, Inception is a film about an adventure. This film also has a very creative background story, and many of the settings in the film is rather novelty. Some people say that this film is very brain-burning and hard to understand. However, I think it is just because the film has lots of high-level factors and it is not easy to understand them. 'Time' is a very important factor in the film (even the theme song of the music is called 'time' too!) . There are different levels of dreams and the time in those dreams are different (just like 'Interstellar'!) . The characters in this film must try to keep the 'falling point' of different levels of dreams happen at the same time, and this is actually a very difficult task. To express this idea to the audiences is also a hard job. However, I think Nolan had done a great job. It is his strength to tell a story that has several timelines, he did excellent well in this film. Every timeline has been shown clearly and the film is tight paced, especially when reaches the back part of the film, the fast switches between different timelines create an exciting atmosphere. The music is also very shocking. At the end of the film, when the characters wake up on the airplane, and the theme music rang, I even wondered whether I'm in the real world or still in a dream!

10.title: Dreams as the Pinnacle of a Movie Theme
10.content:
There has been much said about Inception, which makes it hard to point out it's strength and flaws in a meaningful way. I will just add some thoughts to this masterpiece of a movie (my favorite one by far) here, that are important to me.

First of all, Inception centers about dreams, which is in my honest opinion the one thing, that all movies try to aspire in us: They want to make us dream: "What if?"

Second, Inception makes a compelling heist movie. It sets up its stage and its rules (1/3 of the movie), and then has "one" long suspense, that lasts till the clever end.

Third, Inception gets the feelings right. Nolan - in my opinion - has a tough time conveying emotional characters; the story of Cobb and Mal is bittersweet though.

There are hardly things one can really point out as its weaknesses: Inception has to set its rules straight at the beginning ("exposition") and couldn't have done otherwise. Inception could maybe use a tad less violence (Nolan can seemingly only create movies with violence though) to create suspense. Dreams can involve much more fancy stuff (see Paprika) than just Snow Landscapes and Skyscrapers.

Overall this movie gets so much things right, it is a clear 10/10.

10.title: Inception is a masterpiece that changed cinema forever.
10.content:
Inception is a movie everyone in the world has to watch completely, from start to finish, in the best and most comfortable way possible, at least once in their life. Everyone.

An intense thriller with a unique idea done in a way we've never seen before on screen.

The mere concept of this film is done and portrayed to perfection by Christopher Nolan. In Nolan's own words, the best way to enjoy this movie isn't to understand it but to feel it.

The concept can be confusing, but if you completely focus when watching then I don't think it should be too confusing. Everything made perfect sense to me while watching.

The cinematography in this is incredible. The action is simple but some of the most edge of your seat stuff you'll ever find.

The visuals are amazing, I do not know how Nolan managed to film and even think of some of the things shown here. Nolan captures the notion of dreams so well.

The score by Hans Zimmer is as always of course, outstanding. It's what allows to connect all these crazy and different dreams so well.

The performances were all great, of course the main highlight is Leonardo DiCaprio, he carries the film. But everyone else was great. Two other surprisingly great showing was Cillian Murphy, something about him just makes you so invested and interested in his character. The other is Marion Cotillard, she steals the scene and owns it every time she's in one.

The way this movie is paced and designed is phenomenal, you almost never get a break while watching it. The only time it ever slows down is when the movie ends, and that's done intentionally, we feel the exact same way the characters did in that moment, the experience everyone gets after waking up from a crazy dream.

Overall, one of the best movie experiences I've ever had. Every moment of this film was just so interesting, so well directed and breathtaking.

10.title: The Most original, Thoughtful, and Utterly Great Film
10.content:
**This Review Can Contain Spoilers**

This film is a game-changer. Riding high on the success of "The Dark Knight," Christopher Nolan decided to do this one project that he worked for years on. By God does the result show his dedication! This is one of the most complex films in terms of plot, characters, and motivations. The script not only goes into the mind, it goes into the different layers of each person's mind and does what a fabulous script should do. It throws huge twists, makes some smart story choices, and describes fantastic situations (like Paris folding on top of itself) It is a mortal sin that he did not win the Oscar and was beaten by a bland forgettable film i will not mention (*cough* *cough* The King's Speech)

The cast is beyond exceptional, with one exception. Leonardo DiCaprio gives a knockout performance, as usual. Joseph Gordon-Levitt was excellent, along with the always incredible Ken Watanabe, and a newcomer named Tom Hardy. The rest are equally fine, with Cillian Murphy giving the performance of his lifetime. The one drawback is Ellen Page. After watching her stale performance in Juno, I hoped she would be better here. Not really, but she did help keep the plot moving, credit for that.

The look of this film. One single word, PERFECTION. Nolan uses his regular crew from The Dark Knight, and uses them to an even greater degree. Wally Pfister gives his greatest work as a cinematographer, using different tones and lighting for each level of the mission. The special effects are a breath of fresh air from CGI, hell there is very little CGI, mostly models and gimbals, like the Hallway (one of the best scenes from any movie ever) Hans Zimmer is in top shape, with the track "Time" as his most emotional piece.

I can't talk enough about this movie, it would be a sin for me to reveal any of the plot to anyone. It's really to watch and take it as it unfolds. I would give this film 20/10, but I cannot unfortunately. It was an epiphany for me, showing me that movie can be fun, original, and how much dedication and vision can give the world a movie to treasure forever. It blew me away, and i left the theater cheering.

This Dream Became The Reality for the greatest filmmaker of this generation.

10.title: Leonardo DiCaprio's performance was exceptional.
10.content:
Experiencing this movie was like embarking on an astonishing journey of the mind right from the outset. The opening scene captivated me, as it artfully mirrored the enigmatic nature of dreams themselves. Like finding oneself in a dream without a clear beginning, it effortlessly immersed me into its narrative, akin to being washed ashore in a dreamlike state. This symbolic approach beautifully resonated with the film's ending, leaving viewers questioning the boundaries between reality and Cobb's dreams, as we observed his totem spin. Perhaps it's all part of an intricate dream? This film is an extraordinary event in its own right, and anyone failing to grasp its brilliance simply lacks an understanding of exceptional filmmaking.

This movie stands apart from any other, making it challenging to draw comparisons. Undoubtedly, it has attained legendary status. Needless to say, Leonardo DiCaprio's performance was exceptional. The roles he chooses consistently showcase his talents to perfection, delivering some of the most remarkable acting of our time. His on-screen presence is utterly captivating, effortlessly evoking the precise emotional depth demanded by the character and situation. His expertise is simply unparalleled.

The overarching concept of implanting thoughts or ideas into someone's mind and observing the ensuing consequences was incredibly thought-provoking. The power of this notion left a lasting impression, effectively manifesting throughout the film. This exceptionally intelligent movie refuses to underestimate its audience. It weaves a tapestry of various interwoven plot threads, each vital to the foundation of the storyline. The writing is truly masterful.

I thoroughly enjoyed the exploration of dreams, the different layers within them, and the constant questioning and manipulation of reality. As someone deeply intrigued by such concepts, this movie had me engrossed from beginning to end, carefully avoiding spoilers.

With popcorn at the ready, I embarked on a thrilling cinematic adventure. Let the journey begin! 🍿

10.title: Nolans Masterpiece. A beautiful journey.
10.content:
If you have plan on seeing Christopher Nolan's mind-bending new movie, you should do so quickly, because this is sure to be the type of movie that has people standing around at the local party talking about for months and even years to come. A beautiful masterpiece.

Let me start out by saying that Inception is one of the best movies I have seen this year, and ranks among the best movies I have ever seen. I am not biast towards any director and was a little worried about this although I love Nolans work with deep sci-fi fascination which might make you think that I would be predisposed to liking this movie anyway. Nolan's sci-fi slanted, Beautiful, mind-blowing film is certain to be the type of movie that won't be easily defined, and will appeal to fans of any genre. Years from now, video stores (assuming there are any video stores left years from now) will likely have to think long and hard about whether to label this movie as sci-fi, action, or even drama before assigning it a place on the shelves. It is a movie that defies easy analysis, but still manages to entertain.

Inception is Nolan's reward for the success of the Batman films. Without the critical and commercial success of his previous blockbusters, it is hard to imagine a studio shelling out the kind of money that Warner Bros. handed over to Nolan for what is essentially a passion project- roughly $160 million. By comparison, 2008's The Dark Knight cost $185 million and it was a tested franchise with massive buzz even before the script was finished. Inception is a different kind of animal.

Christopher Nolan has wowed us all again and as I am only 16 and am pleased to know that I will have the amazing privilege of seeing his work in years to come. this mindblowing, action packed thriller has everyone on the end of their seats. I have already seen it three times in the four days it has been out and while some will be screaming at the ending others will agree it is really part of the true beauty of the film and what Christopher Nolan has created down to the slightest detail is a masterpiece. Well done Chrsitopher Nolan you have wowed us all once again.

10.title: Nolan's Masterpiece

10.title: Inception
10.content:
Usually I try to be careful with over hyping a film, or setting the expectations too high, as film geeks all are guilty for, however for Christopher Nolan's Inception, this really is not possible.

This is possibly one of the only perfect films I have ever seen. It is absolutely confident in every way, something which is extremely refreshing, even more so than Avatar. Christopher Nolan gets some slack for making great to look at but ultimately heartless affairs, which I for one do not agree with, however I do not think anyone can argue that here. The emotional aspect of this film not only ties it all together but is really the centre of this film, it is the focus.

I do not want to over simplify the film, by simply calling it Kubrick doing Bond, or Gondry on a huge budget, because I am sure it will be called that but it is far more than that, it is something I do not think Kubrick could have ever made. It is pure Nolan, and pure greatness.

I hate writing something which is pure fan-boy gushing, but its really difficult here. I did not find a thing I did not like about it, I am sure if maybe I saw it a second time, maybe I would find something about it I didn't like, but not the first time. The way it is cut, means that there is always action on screen, if not, then the visuals are interesting enough to keep your eyes glued.

The final hour of the film, is possibly one of the most complicated action sequences put on film. You have to constantly be paying attention to remember all of the layers of what is happening. Without spoiling anything, all I have to say is that is what this film is about, that is what makes this film so great, layers. Once you have seen this you will now what I am talking about.

All of the actors are fantastic too, Di Caprio is the stand out here. Yes, this is probably due to the fact he is the star and given all of the emotional weight, but he handles it perfectly, similarly to his performance in Shutter Island. Ellen Page, whom I usually hate, gives a great performance here. Tom Hardy gives a break out performance here, he is quite the bad ass.

I hope audiences are ready for a film like this, a pure auteur driven film which does not sacrifice a single frame for the studio. I would hope this film will change Hollywood, as it is 100 percent the directors vision yet it is definitely a marketable film, much like District 9, yet I do not think it will.

I cannot recommend this film anymore than I have, I just have to say everyone and anyone should see it. Sorry about all the gushing, it is just so hard not too.

10.title: Classic Nolan
10.content:
Inception is art. Everything from the cinematography to the poetic way the plot revolves. Everything about Inception is brilliant. Nolan manages to achieve his unrivalled combination of tasteful action and beautiful artistry again as he has done in so many of his movies now and that's what sets him aside. It is incredible how this movie juggles the introduction to so many characters to well. This is especially prevalent as we've seen many film blunder from having too many characters. The movie has a clear set of rules, which it never breaks. This makes it feel smart without even considering the genius concept the whole movie is based on! In my opinion this is arguably the best idea for a screenplay ever. Leonardo DiCaprio is...well, Leonardo DiCaprio, need I say anymore? His performance easily outlines his ideas with ease. The one main flaw talked about in this movie is the amount of exposition. Yes there is a lot of exposition to get to the main plot, however the genius is that Nolan will smoothen out the exposition by having the landscape fall in on itself or something miraculous like that. Which leads me to to the visual effects and score. Hans Zimmer has smashed it again with a gorgeously composed score perfect to set the tone for any scene. The visual effects are obviously stunning, so much so they've been almost a staple of the 2010s action movie. Referenced in doctor Strange and other movies. And if you haven't seen one of these effects, be it a spinning corridor or again, Paris flipped on its head, you've been sitting under a rock for 10 years. The script also has a bounce and poetic feel to it and the rest of the cast execute it beautifully The outro, with little to no words is an exhibition in wordless story telling and leaving it in total ambiguity like that is a key talking point that will be referenced like the end of terminator 2 or a new Hope.

A Nolan extraordinaire 10/10

10.title: The Nolan Experience Continues
10.content:
I saw somebody say that this is Nolan's first true masterpiece. That might be true, but I believe this is only his second original work. Therefore, I think it is not so bold to say there is room for many more.

When I saw Memento, I knew that I was experiencing a whole new kind of director. One that was not only brilliant, skilled, original, and stylish; but also British. I love it when a director is British as it helps me to believe that one day it could be me.

Inception is so dense in plot; so wrapped in layers that will only become apparent with multiple watches; and so visually well presented, I am in no way surprised it tops the list of greatest movies of all time.

For some reason I tend to feel as though no modern movie should ever be awarded with such an honour: but it should, because every movie was modern once, and Christopher Nolan is a director who should be celebrated on every level. For what the man has done for batman alone he should be knighted.

Well done Christopher Nolan, you amaze me with everything you do, please continue to delve into my mind and make me like you as much as you wish. Well... steady how you go.

10.title: I just made myself a totem
10.content:
Inception is a film best delivered cold...that meaning, the less you know about it going in, the more you'll cling to the edge of your seats!

Nolan delivers again in this mind-boggling, action-adventure film. It challenges both your mind and instinct, to trust your OWN mind that the scene you're watching is taking place in whatever level of dream (or reality) the characters may "say" they are in.

You don't have to over-analyze this movie to watch it, but also don't sit back and let it wash over you...you will miss huge clues along the way.

The best way to enjoy this film is by, well, staying focused. Check the time, take off your sweater; anything...and you could just miss the clue to an entire 45 minutes of viewing. This film demands your full attention and if you give it to it, you will come out of the theatre with a big grin on your face expressing your "wow" and "amazement".

This film gets a perfect 10 from me. Acting was superb and plot was engaging and astounding to say the least. The story sucks you in and drops you out with a whole new look at the film.

This is something you don't want to miss.

10.title: I quibble, but this is a really good film for the alert layman
10.content:
*******Continuous Spoiler Alerts ***********

This review is intended ONLY for people who have seen the film once.

If you have not seen the film, please see the film and do not read any reviews or watch the trailer and literally close your eyes / turn off the TV if the trailer comes on. The less you know, the better.

This is a good film.

I saw the ending coming. But the "13th Floor" is a better version of the same "topic", but my guess is that non-computer people could not understand the concept of a VM (a virtual machine), which I have dealt with as a computer programmer since (gasp) 1975.

As bebop987 said, "If you liked Nolan's previous films "Memento",  you will love Inception". However, I disagree with that reviewer who goes on to say "Deep down this film is about forgiveness and letting go but also has a great scifi sheen that never takes that idea away." I feel it is about forgiveness of others and of self, but there are simplicities / dumbing down of the concept compared to "13th floor".

For some reason, I'm getting to dislike Joseph Gordon-Levitt, perhaps because of a string of movies he did several years ago that were the same character re-packaged. But truly, that's minor (Sorry JGL).

I like the idea of recruitment of a student Ariadne (Page) who takes it up a notch (Bam, to quote the Chef Emeril Lagasse, and does so a little like Keanu Reeves in "Matrix" (part 1 in 1999). However, Matrix 1 is a better movie than this, in that it is so immersive, that in Matrix 1, you feel as if you may have the powers to make things bend and walk through traffic (scary, but literally true when a friend and I saw the movie in the same cinema).

I also agree (word for word) with tmldtt who says: "The story is tense, deep and disturbing. The tension is taut and it hardly ever slackens. The dreams within dreams within dreams concept is complex to say the least. It requires complete attention from the viewer if he wants to decipher every little puzzle the movie throws. The acting is top-notch." And I agree with mblueyesm who writes "And I think it does NOT stop spinning in the end!... Brilliant!!"

However, I start my review with the title "this is a really good film for the alert layman", and add to it (so I don't spoil it for others), for the psychologists/psychiatrists who listen to dreams: I hope you doc's see it before reading anything about it.

Let me go back to "The 13th Floor (1999)". In it, there is a dream within a dream. But the ending has another level dream: essentially the same story as Inception, but using dreams (which everyone has) instead of computers and virtual machines which perhaps 1-5% of the population has. And that's the difference: director Nolan took a hot concept, and popularized it in a subtle and graceful way. Kudos, Mr. Nolan. But, sadly, the trailers let me see the key parts and the ending even though I studiously (and seriously) avoided all mentions of Inception before seeing it on opening weekend (I was too tired to see the movie on Fri, 7/16/2010 – and was scared to see it under the influence of anything for fear of getting nightmares).

TMI: Too Much Information: I happen to be one of those people who have realistic controlled dreams, known as "lucid dreaming." Here are two definitions of Lucid Dreaming:

1. 'Lucid dreaming is more than just controlled dreams' ... 'Many people report "their first lucid dream was the most wonderful experience of their lives" (LaBerge: 1997). '

serendip.brynmawr.edu/exchange/node/1759

2. "A lucid dream is a dream in which the sleeper is aware that he or she is dreaming. A lucid dreamer can actively participate in and manipulate imaginary experiences in the dream environment. Lucid dreams can seem extremely real and vivid, depending on a person's level of self-awareness during the lucid dream.

The term was coined by the Dutch psychiatrist and writer Frederik van Eeden (1860–1932)."

en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucid_dream

In lucid dreams (I'm speaking about mine), I can fly away when in danger, and recognize (rarely) that I'm in a dream. I sometimes think: "wow, I'm flying away, so this must be a dream". As a kid, I wanted to fly: just like The Pee-wee Herman Show (1981). Gee, I'm dating myself with a 29 year old film reference. A "Hot in Cleveland" Cougar dates a guy 15 years younger, and she mentions a TV show (I believe), the younger guy says "I love re-runs" when she (and I) clearly saw it when it came out.

So, given my lucid dreaming, I could, if the film were reality,

1) totally adapt to the Inception world view,

2a) sadly could see myself addicted to this sleep drug (as poor Michael Jackson was with propofol)

2b) Leonardo's character was with not having REM sleep--driving you mad, a nice touch from Nolan -- also: StarTrek's episode "Night Terrors" (1991).

3) the poor 12 individuals druggist's basement.

A Playboy scifi story (circa 1960's) has a box connected to the brain's pleasure center which people easily bypass the safety feature & have it on continuously for days, dying in their chairs, with the sweet smell of their rotting flesh from not having gotten up to eat. I sure hope that is not the future of mankind. Addictive and forces you into a lifestyle that in a sense enslaves you: hopefully an illegal effect.

So, Director/writer Nolan did a great job combining science, fears, dreams, elaborate set designs, and computer theory / simulations (using a simulation to eliminate gravity and laws of physics, which is now standard, but is beyond what I can do on a computer).

10.title: The Masterpiece of our generation
10.content:
Inception is undoubtedly the best movie ever made! The Masterpiece of our generation. It truly one of a kind. A concept which has long gestated in Christopher Nolan's mind, his eye for drama mixed with his large scale sensibilities ring true in Blockbuster season making Inception a true original in the sea of reboots, remakes and sequels.

Inception has the capacity to blow you away.Just like the classics of decades gone by,namely The Godfather movies and movies by the likes of Scorcese and Scott, this movie is the classic of our generation and Nolan truly deserves his place among the elite.

The movie has a scintillating pace throughout and the premise despite being far-fetched has a believable quality to it thanks to some amazing performances and intelligent direction.

The viewer is immediately thrown into Nolan's world of corporate espionage and extraction of "ideas".The editing is magnificent as the audience is often subjected to following multiple narratives without losing connection with the plot.There is a lot of craft involved in revealing just about enough at just the right time to keep you on the edge.Once the movie pushes into the triple-dream-layer sequence one cannot help but gape in astonishment at how mind boggling special- effects are seamlessly combined with the intricacies of the plot.The climax,quite simply, takes your breath away just like the climaxes of earlier Nolan films like "Following" and "The Dark Knight".

The performances are commendable and one wonders how Nolan always seems to get his casting perfectly apt.Leonardo DiCaprio has evolved so much from the days of "Titanic".His role,though similar to the one he played in "Shutter Island", evokes sympathy for the man whose inner guilt poses the greatest hazard to the mission.Its a balanced performance and his scenes with Marion Cotillard are terrific.Joseph Gordon-Levitt is a pleasant surprise turning in a very neat job with his portrayal of Arthur.Ken Watanabe is quite classy and exudes panache throughout.Tom Hardy and Ellen Page play their parts well.But the one to look out for is Cillian Murphy.In his role of an heir to a billionaire oil tycoon,he excels in bringing out the torment and angst associated with living in the shadow of his father.Michael Caine though, is a bit underused and one always yearns to see more of him.

Hanz Zimmer has once again emerged with a winning score which completely takes over the movie in the final few minutes and pushes the climax a few notches higher.The undertone is a tad similar to the one used in "Shutter Island" but one enjoys the ominous music as it lends a certain gravity to the overall mood.

All in all, if you watch it once,you will watch it again.And then again.And again.Because each viewing offers something new.Something extra.

When I saw "The Dark Knight", I said to myself that Nolan has truly reached his pinnacle and that this here is his masterpiece.Its a pity that I did not check my totem then.I must have been dreaming!

10.title: Inception is not just a film
10.content:
Inception, directed by the visionary Christopher Nolan, is an extraordinary masterpiece that transcends the boundaries of traditional cinema. This mind-bending tour de force pushes the limits of storytelling, visuals, and intellectual engagement, resulting in a cinematic experience like no other. With its profound exploration of the human mind and its labyrinthine narrative, Inception stands as a testament to the power of cinema to captivate and challenge its audience.

One of the film's greatest achievements is its exceptionally intricate and multilayered screenplay. Nolan, known for his penchant for complex narratives, weaves a gripping tale of dreams within dreams, blurring the lines between reality and imagination. The script is a marvel of craftsmanship, seamlessly interconnecting different levels of consciousness while maintaining an astonishing level of coherence. This intricate structure not only serves as a testament to Nolan's creative genius but also keeps the audience enthralled, constantly questioning their own perceptions.

The performances in Inception are nothing short of extraordinary. Leonardo DiCaprio delivers a tour de force as Dom Cobb, a troubled yet determined thief who specializes in the art of extraction. DiCaprio's portrayal is filled with emotional depth and intensity, capturing the inner conflicts and complexities of his character with unwavering conviction. The ensemble cast, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, and Tom Hardy, each brings their A-game, elevating the film to new heights. Their chemistry and commitment to their roles create a palpable sense of camaraderie and tension throughout the narrative.

Visually, Inception is a feast for the eyes. Nolan's meticulous attention to detail is evident in every frame, as he seamlessly blends practical effects with cutting-edge CGI. From gravity-defying fight scenes in a rotating hallway to the breathtaking cityscapes folding in on themselves, the film's visual effects are nothing short of awe-inspiring. The stunning cinematography by Wally Pfister adds to the film's overall grandeur, capturing both the ethereal beauty of dreams and the gritty reality of the subconscious.

Inception is not merely a visual spectacle but also a film that delves deep into existential themes and philosophical questions. It explores the nature of reality, the power of memory, and the indomitable human spirit. The film's layers of meaning invite introspection and invite audiences to ponder the boundaries of perception and the fragility of our own constructed realities.

Hans Zimmer's haunting and evocative score perfectly complements the film's narrative, elevating the emotional resonance of every scene. The pulsating rhythm and crescendos of Zimmer's music create a sense of urgency and tension, intensifying the already gripping storytelling.

Inception is a testament to the power of ambitious filmmaking. Christopher Nolan has crafted a visionary masterpiece that challenges our notions of reality, perception, and consciousness. It combines breathtaking visuals, a labyrinthine narrative, and exceptional performances to create an unforgettable cinematic experience. It's a film that demands multiple viewings to fully appreciate its intricacies, and each revisit rewards the audience with new layers of understanding.

Inception is not just a film; it's a bold and daring exploration of the human mind and its infinite possibilities. It will leave you in a state of awe and wonder long after the credits roll. Christopher Nolan has once again proven himself as a master storyteller, and Inception will undoubtedly stand the test of time as one of the greatest achievements in cinematic history.

10.title: Inception: Ten Years Young
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" (2010) is back in cinemas ahead of the release of "Tenet", and for its 10th anniversary.

It's amazing that Inception is 10 years old. Have I been dreaming? Has time slowed down? As this classic came out before I started One Mann's Movies, a review of this tenth anniversary showing seems justified.

It's no surprise this get a solid 10*s from me. What surprised me more was how INCREDIBLE it is to see this on a really big screen again... and with really great sound.

There are so many standout moments to call out:



It's a cast to die for. Leonardo diCaprio as Cobb leads the cast with strong support - REALLY strong support - from the ensemble cast. Of that cast the acts, that standout are Ken Watanabe as Saito, Ellen Page as Ariadne and, particularly, Marion Cottilard as Cobb's dead wife Mal. Both Tom Hardy and Joseph Gordon-Levitt are great, but come over a bit too cocky and smug on repeat watches!

The old Nolan favourite - Michael Caine as Cobb's kid's grandfather (I don't think it's ever mentioned whether he is Cobb Snr). (Source: Warner Brothers).

What makes the movie so compelling for me is not all of the whiz-bang practical effects, but the emotional wallop of the backstory between Cobb and his wife Mal. As the film digs deeper and deeper, so that emotional story intensifies: growing old together for over 50 years; wrinkled hand holding wrinkled hand. GULP.

Blend that with his need of Cobb to see the faces of his children again - Nolan constantly teasing us with the prospect - and it drives the movie along at a completely different level of quality.

It comes down to a personal preference. But there are a number of Christopher Nolan candidates that might make your list of his best films: "Memento"? "The Dark Knight"? "Interstellar"? Perhaps for some people now (not me personally) "Tenet"? But for me, "Inception" is his high-water mark of quality, and firmly in my top 10 favourite films of all time.

10.title: An original and thrilling blockbuster spectacle
10.content:
A flawed masterpiece that offers ample chances for viewers to pick holes in various plot points or instances, Inception is also one of the most ambitious and memorable pieces of blockbuster filmmaking of the last decade and a film that solidified Christopher Nolan as the king of large-scale Summer fair offerings that offers audiences the chance to witness unique and visually grandiose cinema that is rare to find in today's climate.

Brash, loud and mostly enthralling, Inception takes us on a wild ride into the world of dreams, deceptions and big life questions as we follow Leonardo DiCaprio's dream time conman Dom Cobb and his crack team of sidekicks as they look to pull off a daring "inception" heist on a high-profile target that will test the very nature of what is possible as their mission takes them deep into the subconscious of the unknown.

It's a plotline that only Nolan could pull off, similar to the mind-melting feats of Interstellar, Memento and The Prestige, Inception takes multiple viewings to fully appreciate and while its plot contrivances and plot holes become more aware on repeat screenings (Cobbs relationship with deceased wife Mal can become frustrating as does the films self-indulgent finale), the highs of Inception far outweigh any of the instances that disappoint, helping create a film that is well deserving of its place deep inside the Top 250 films of all-time on movie bible website IMDB.

From the moment the film starts and we see Cobb washed ashore on a mysterious beach, through to such eye-popping and white-knuckle moments as the city of Paris literally turning in on itself or Joseph Gordon-Levitt's Arthur flying around in a zero gravity hotel hallway fighting off a generic goon, Inception offers up spectacle and intrigue like very films can dare dream to do and with Nolan's insistence on going practical wherever possible, there are numerous moments throughout his big-budget affair that you can't help but be astounded by.

Near 10 years on from release, Nolan's ability to craft such a technically sound production ensure that Inception has lost none of its initial charms and for anyone that has bypassed for the film in the last decade, it's safe to say that Inception is one of those rare breeds of film that feels ageless in a time and place where many other high-profile picks fail to stand up to the test of time.

Inception is also one of Nolan's most purely playful and fun films, a heist film done that way of hijacked dreams and acts of deception, you sense the giddiness and joy Nolan would've had conjuring up this film into a reality and never a director to do things the easy way, this is the perfect example of a high-concept feature done with thoughtfulness and tact but also with entertaining at the forefront of its mantra and for those that are willing to be swept away by Nolan's grand vision that's lead by a typically strong DiCaprio turn, Inception is about as good as it gets in regards to big-scale movie making.

Final Say -

Likely to remain a film that is talked about and debated about for the years yet to come, Inception has its flaws should you care to look but at the end of the day Nolan's wild ride into the depths of the human subconscious is just as joyous too behold now as it was on the big screen all those years ago.

5 grenade launchers out of 5

10.title: I never get tired of it!!
10.content:
Overview

Cobb(Leonardo DiCaprio) is a spy who steals corporate secrets through dream-sharing technology which allows him to enter the targets' dreams and extracts their ideas or secrets from within their dreams. Saito(Ken Watanabe) offered him an extremely difficult mission to lead his competitor who monopolizes the industry, to ruin. He suggested "inception" to Cobb, which means planting an idea in someone's mind, even though it's thought to be impossible. If the mission is successful, Saito promises that he is going to help Cobb get back to his children because Cobb has been charged with his wife's murder and expelled from the country. Cobb accepted Saito's offer and decided to try to do "inception" with his team, but Cobb had a secret which he didn't tell to anyone and related to "inception".

Review

"Inception" has consistently stayed in my TOP3 of all time even though I've watched more than 600 movies so far. The director of this movie, Nolan is one of my favorite directors. He is really good at manipulating our expectations of chronological order. I was amazed by the idea of Inception, how he was able to imagine thinking of such a well-organized story line. This movie reached the pinnacle of storytelling in movies. In the dream that Cobb and his team are in, they designed the structure of the places. The dream has three layers, and for each layer they go down, the time passes more slowly. They took advantage of that, and tried to plant the idea in the target's mind as deep as possible for it to stitch naturally. I'm pretty sure the structure and storyline are both perfect. The actor's performance was also amazing. Leo performed great, as usual, even though he portrayed a difficult character and other actors also acted really well. In addition, the score of this movie was fantastic because Hans Zimmer who has been nominated for an Oscar more than ten times and others created the score. Inception is an intricate movie, but I love it! I've watched it at least ten times, but it never disappoints me and I never get tired of it. I finally watched it in the theater in IMAX and 4DX because they recently re-released it. Watching this movie in the theater was on my bucket-list. I don't know how to express how much I love this movie.

10.title: chuang chou dreaming a butterfly
10.content:
Director Nolan's "Inception" turned out that there was a person on the other end of the Earth who had the same strange idea for many years. This time Nolan expanded this idea even further by cleverly adding a gyroscope, which determines whether the protagonists are in reality or in dreams. Of course, there is also the child's face, and this scene has appeared more than once in the film - in the dream, Cobb will never see his own child's face. Do we also have such an experience? Many scenes appear more than once in dreams, but we can never touch the results. For this reason, I am extremely amazed by the director's imagination. Through excellent narrative techniques, Nolan has "implanted" his understanding of dreams into our brains, resonating in our hearts.

In the film, the director raises a profound philosophical question for us - does the real world we perceive really exist? Are all the things in our dreams fake? The starting point of this philosophical proposition is the most fundamental and thorough suspicion of human cognitive ability. Descartes once described the beginning of his thought process as follows: "Everything that I think is closest to 'reality' so far comes from feelings and the communication of feelings. However, I have found that these things often deceive us. Therefore, the only wise thing is to no longer fully believe what the eyes see.

In the film, Cobb kept doubting everything until he truly saw the smiling face of his child turning around. At the end of the film, I suddenly remembered a philosophical enlightenment book I had read many years ago - "Sophie's World": a little girl named Sophie accidentally met someone who took her into a dream where Sophie met various philosophical sages from ancient to modern times and sensed their thoughts. In this dream, Sophie continued to grow and become more rational. Until one day Sophie walked to a small house in the wilderness and opened the door, placing a mirror in front of her. In the mirror, it wasn't Sophie's face, but another illusion. Sophie kept asking if everything around her was real. This question continued until the end of the book, where it was written: 'With a loud bang, we are all stars.' Is that what director Christopher Nolan wants to tell us?

Cobb is offered a chance to have his criminal record erased in exchange for planting an idea in someone's mind, a process known as "inception." Praised for its innovative narrative, stunning visual effects, and strong performances, "Inception" is celebrated as a thought-provoking and visually stunning cinematic experience.

10.title: A Mind-Bending Masterpiece: Inception Redefines the Boundaries of Cinema

Inception, directed by Christopher Nolan, is an extraordinary cinematic achievement that will leave you spellbound. From its mind-bending concept to its exceptional execution, the film pushes the boundaries of storytelling and takes the audience on an exhilarating journey through dreams and reality. Nolan's masterful direction, coupled with a stellar ensemble cast led by Leonardo DiCaprio, delivers a gripping and emotionally charged narrative that keeps you on the edge of your seat.

Visually stunning and intellectually stimulating, Inception is a true cinematic masterpiece. The film's breathtaking visuals, intricate set pieces, and seamless blend of practical and visual effects create a mesmerizing dreamscape that blurs the lines between what is real and what is imagined. With its thought-provoking themes of perception, memory, and the power of the subconscious, Inception invites audiences to contemplate the nature of reality long after the credits roll. 10.title: Step into this Inception
10.content:
After a very strong 'The Dark Knight' it seem to be impossible for Nolan to create a more intriguing story and plot. As this modern director knows what he's holding in his hands, he slides you into an imaginary world where you believe it can be true. Everything is being portrait in details and very real. This combined with a imaginary fantasy idea that we can go into other people's dreams, sounds an easy story line, but it's the whole road that makes this movie so different and perfect.

Starting with the script. The idea is already something where you can talk about a lot... what is happening in your dreams and how do you control it? Than Nolan manages to create this whole emotional story, which is the ground base of the movie... Can you control your dreams? Adventually he gives the main characters a choice, depending on the viewers that they will follow this character into the plot... do you want to control your dreams?

You also have the genuine and perfect acting performances. DiCaprio gets to another level with this performance, Cotillard gives an extra impulse to the story and manages to surprise us again, Page doses her emotions more & more and is credible in her role, Gordon-Levitt performs one of the most impossible scenes in movie history and gets away with it,... All these acting performances (how small or how big they even are), are very matched to each other.

The music is bombastic and subtle at the right moment... Hans Zimmer will be a very strong contender for an Oscar. It lifts some scenes even more to a floating level.

The FX are near to perfect, scene with DiCaprio/Page at a Paris Café is something you have to watch over and over again. It pops The Matrix into another dimension.

But most of all, it's all about the producing and directing this movie, and that's where Nolan comes in (again). This man not only deserves an Oscar nomination (after already some near to perfect movies like 'The Dark Knight', 'Memento' & 'Batman Begins'), he is a genuine artist with lots of stories to tell and brings us entertainment from another, exciting level. A level we needed after all those years with all those superhero movies, sequels & remakes. Thank you Nolan, crew & cast... and don't you dare NOT to see this movie... It will be one of your favourites for sure!

10.title: Christopher Nolan's Vision
10.content:
Few careers are as remarkably unique as Christopher Nolan's: in only 12 years he's moved from the likes of Following, his debut feature which was shot during weekends for over a year, to Batman Begins and The Dark Knight, movies that transcend their "genre" roots and become great pieces of drama and cinema, conquering critics, awards and audiences (a billion dollars and counting for The Dark Knight). And in between these bigger projects, there are smart, compelling works like Memento and The Prestige, expert lessons in storytelling and filmmaking that, on some levels, are as much about Nolan himself as they are about the characters populating those fictional universes. And then there's Inception, a rarity among summer blockbusters in that it has a considerable budget (close to 200 million dollars), but also an intelligent, layered script which demands attention from the viewer (though not quite to the same degree as, say, The Matrix). It is also, arguably up to this point, Nolan's magnum opus.

Given the director's secretive attitude throughout production, the less said about the plot, the better, apart from some basic information: The main character, Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), is a man who specializes in stealing elements from other people's dreams, thanks to a technique he has perfected over the years and a team of accomplices (Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page and Tom Hardy, among others). He's also haunted by visions of his dead wife (Marion Cotillard) and some dark secrets that prevent him from going back home. Then one day he is asked to do the opposite of his standard MO: this time, he has to plant an idea into the subject's mind. No longer extraction, but inception...

From the start, it is clear that Inception is far from the average sci-fi thriller: the opening act alone is a masterclass in narrative deception, thanks in no small part to Nolan's decision to avoid any visual gimmicks - color or format shifts - to separate the real world from the dream-scape. The truth is in the most minute details, and spotting them isn't easy. If The Prestige was a not-so-subtle metaphor for Nolan's filmmaking (the structure of the magic trick mirrored his handling of the plot), the concept is taken even further in Inception, where the maze (i.e. the layout of the dream) constructed by Page's Ariadne (a highly symbolic name, taken from Greek mythology), reflects the director's visual storytelling, with a masterful use of inter-cuts and music to guide us through his own cinematic labyrinth.

At the same time, the film also has to deliver on the action level, and it truly does: this is equal parts Memento (each scene clarifies or even contradicts the previous one) and Batman Begins (a fact that is slyly referenced in the casting of Ken Watanabe, Cillian Murphy and Michael Caine), with explosions, chases and shootouts that complete the story rather than being autonomous bits of film. From an impressive hotel set-piece that bears comparison with The Matrix (the big difference being that Nolan uses CGI as sparingly as possible) to the magnificent shot of a street defying the laws of physics, everything serves the story and its dream-like scope (the real reason Nolan waited almost a decade to actually make a film). As for the movie's human center, a necessary element to make the whole thing work on an emotional level, the doomed romance between Cobb (a superb DiCaprio who just keeps getting better) and his wife (kudos to Cotillard for giving such soul to a character that isn't, strictly speaking, real), is the summation of the director's filmography, from Memento to The Dark Knight via The Prestige: amidst all the spectacle and philosophy, it's the people that matter.

Inception is with no doubt one of the year's - heck, even the decade's - best films, complex but also hugely exciting and rewarding, a piece of work that stimulates eyes, brain and heart and also embodies the essence of Stanley Kubrick's famed view on cinema: watching a movie is like dreaming.

10.title: Nolan's done it again!!
10.content:
I honestly couldn't have gone into a cinema with higher expectations, and I can openly admit that I didn't expect Inception to come even close to the bar I had set it, but, against all odds, it succeeded with flying colours.

Inception is the story of a tormented man, Dom Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), who with a team of experts, uses the technology they have to enter the subconscious mind, and steal the ideas that lie there, for money. So basically, a sci-fi type heist gang. Which, on paper, sounds intriguing, if but a little silly.

However, Christopher Nolan pulls it off here with such a tremendous amount of energy and a somewhat complex although beautiful plot. The last hour in particular is literally incredible, I can say with full certainty that even a science fiction hater, will be on the edge of their seat. For me personally, it was the terrific blend of Cobb's forgotten life, the stunning special effects and the psychological essence that combines to make just an amazing movie.

I know the film will be criticised for the idea of it trying to be the next Matix where reality is not all as it's seems. However, it is not like that at all, and Inception is entirely it's own movie, with it's own plot and set of characters who you emphasise with. In particular, I thought the cast did portray all their roles very effectively, with Marion Cottilard portraying Cobb's estranged wife Mal beautifully, as does DiCaprio, although he does need to spend less time frowning. I also think Joseph Gordon- Levitt and Cillian Murphury portray their roles effectively too.

On the downside, Ellen Page is simply not convincing enough to take on the complexity of her character, as she just feels too young and inexperienced to play the clever Ariadane. I also have to admit that a few times the story does cross the line between complex but hooking, to a little silly, but it always manages to bounce back to keeping you on the ball again.

But overall, it is one of the best, most fascinating, and down right incredible movies I have seen in a long time, and I just have to say well done to Christopher Nolan to creating such a masterpiece, and it is amazing to see a person who just manages to get better an better with each movie he makes.

Re: If you GET KILLED in a dream you wake up, or you don't; When you are heavily sedated you won't wake up, you will go into another dream...if you forget you are in a dream, you will just keep living your life till someone gets you and reminds you, or "jolts" you from the outside. 10.title: Inception
10.content: In Inception, we are taken on a deep and highly illustrated exploration into the field of technologically assisted lucid dreaming, dream communication, and the subconscious mind. After seeing this movie for the first time in the theaters, I have seen it two more times, and with every subsequent viewing, I have been able to understand the concepts even more. Throughout the movie there is talk of a technique named "inception" which can be used to implant messages into certain people's subconscious mind during a certain stage of sleep, hence the tittle of the movie. A fascinating aspect of this movie is the premise of a person being able to communicate with another person while both of them are in a dreaming state of consciousness. On top of that this film explores the different varying levels of dream states and how factors in the physical environment outside of the dreamer translate into factors in the dreamer's lucid dream or subconscious. After doing personal research on the topic of lucid dreaming & the inception of lucid dreams, I have found out that there ACTUALLY ARE a variety of technological instruments which have been developed which are capable of achieving some of the results(or results similar to those) which were achieved in the movie. Thus, Inception is not a total work of fiction or science fiction, but also a reference to what can be and/or is possible to an extent with technology that is currently available or which may be available sometime in the near future. As a person particularly interested in the fields of Parapsychology, Dreamwork, & Psychology, Inception is no doubt a classic production in my eyes.

At its core, Inception is a heist film like no other. However, instead of robbing banks or jewels, the protagonists delve into the subconscious minds of their targets to plant ideas or extract secrets. The concept of dream infiltration is brilliantly realized, offering a fresh take on the genre and allowing for boundless creativity in the narrative.

What sets Inception apart is its meticulous attention to detail. Nolan's screenplay is a marvel of complexity, weaving together multiple layers of reality with precision and clarity. Each dream level is meticulously crafted, from the gravity-defying streets of Paris to the snow-capped peaks of a mountain fortress. The seamless blending of practical effects and CGI creates a surreal yet believable world that draws viewers deeper into the story.

The ensemble cast delivers outstanding performances across the board. Leonardo DiCaprio anchors the film as Dom Cobb, a skilled extractor haunted by his past. His portrayal is both charismatic and haunted, capturing the emotional complexity of a man torn between his desires and his demons. Supporting actors such as Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, and Tom Hardy bring depth and nuance to their respective roles, adding layers of intrigue to the ensemble.

We needed maybe 5.

Otherwise, it's the kind of movie that I wanted to make when I moved to L.A. three years ago -- a stunningly brilliant psychological thriller.

John Lennon said that he couldn't listen to the radio sometimes because when he listened to a great song he was driven mad with envy because he wished he wrote it. I am not comparing myself to Lennon in a movie sense, but as a small-time filmmaker, I understood that feeling when I watched "Inception." I doubt that I will watch anything that comes close to matching its greatness during the next 5 years, and I am astounded and pleased that the public received it so well. I thought that the masses were permanently stuck on wanting something as juvenile and basic as Avatar.

10.title: A Mind-Bending Cinematic Masterpiece
10.content:
"Inception," directed by Christopher Nolan, is a thought-provoking science fiction film that takes audiences on a mesmerizing journey through the depths of dreams. Released in 2010, this cinematic masterpiece continues to captivate viewers with its intricate plot, stunning visuals, and a stellar ensemble cast. With its mind-bending concept and profound exploration of the human psyche, "Inception" stands as one of the most memorable and intellectually stimulating films of its time.

Plot and Concept: The film revolves around Dom Cobb, portrayed brilliantly by Leonardo DiCaprio, an expert in the art of extraction - stealing valuable information from the subconscious of individuals through their dreams. However, Cobb is presented with a unique opportunity to reverse his role and perform "inception" - planting an idea in someone's mind rather than extracting one. This sets the stage for an exhilarating adventure where dreams within dreams become a reality.

The concept of dreams within dreams is executed flawlessly in "Inception." The film skillfully explores the layers of the subconscious, blurring the lines between reality and imagination. As the characters delve deeper into the dream world, the audience is continually kept on edge, unsure of what is real and what is merely a construct of the mind. This complex and thought-provoking narrative is a testament to Nolan's exceptional storytelling abilities.

Visuals and Cinematography: Visually, "Inception" is a feast for the eyes. The film seamlessly transitions between different dream levels, each with its distinct visual style. From a gravity-defying hotel corridor fight scene to the folding cityscape, the visual effects are nothing short of breathtaking. The use of practical effects combined with cutting-edge CGI creates a surreal and immersive experience that draws the viewers into the dreamscapes alongside the characters.

Nolan's choice of practical effects over heavy reliance on CGI adds a tangible quality to the film. The attention to detail is evident in every frame, making even the most outlandish dreams feel palpable. The cinematography by Wally Pfister is exceptional, capturing the grandeur and intensity of each scene with precision. The film's stunning visuals are not just for aesthetic purposes but serve to enhance the narrative and deepen the sense of wonder and intrigue.

Characters and Performances: The ensemble cast of "Inception" delivers remarkable performances, bringing depth and emotional resonance to their respective roles. Leonardo DiCaprio shines as Dom Cobb, a haunted and complex protagonist grappling with his own demons. DiCaprio effortlessly captures the essence of Cobb's tormented soul, allowing the audience to empathize with his motivations and inner conflicts.

Supporting performances by Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, Marion Cotillard, and Ken Watanabe are equally commendable. Each actor breathes life into their characters, adding layers of complexity and nuance. The chemistry between the cast members is palpable, enhancing the authenticity of their relationships within the narrative.

Themes and Philosophy: Beyond its mind-bending narrative and stunning visuals, "Inception" delves into profound philosophical themes. The exploration of dreams, reality, and the power of ideas raises questions about the nature of perception, memory, and the human mind. The film challenges our understanding of what is real and urges viewers to contemplate the impact of our thoughts and beliefs on our lives.

Furthermore, "Inception" touches upon themes of guilt, redemption, and the pursuit of catharsis. Cobb's emotional journey becomes a central focus, weaving together his personal story with the larger themes of the film. This emotional depth adds another layer of resonance to an already intellectually stimulating narrative.

Conclusion: "Inception" is a cinematic triumph that engages its audience on multiple levels. Christopher Nolan's visionary direction, coupled with outstanding performances.

10.title: Another Great Film From Nolan.
10.content: Inception is, in my opinion, one of the most fantastically written and directed films of our time. It has made Nolan one of the most talented directors, (of course, along with the new batman films, memento, and insomnia). I'll give you an explanation of the film, and try not to give away any plot points. It stars Leonardo Di Caprio and Joseph Gordon Levitt as dream "extractors" - talking about how the most resilient parasite is an idea - highly contagious - once it is in the brain, it is impossible to eradicate. The dream extractors steal these ideas. They can search minds and find secrets of the person, however, they must be completely open to the extractors. As if their mind is a safe, and the dream is what is in there - the extractors are trying to steal what is in the safe. The best way to obtain these ideas is going into a dream, in which they go into another dream. So a dream within a dream. Sometimes further, but it is harder to get out of these dreams. Timings are everything. Most people in the dreams are just projections of the mind, random people you may have seen before. However, Di Caprio's character, Cobb, is plagued by his ex-wife; she and him used to have dreams together about their life - they built a world in their dreams, and one day, Cobb planted just a simple idea in her mind that the world wasn't real - spinning a totem, and locking it in a physical, rather than mental, safe. What he did, by planting the idea int a dream to affect the person, is what is known as "Inception". The idea must first be stripped down to it's very basics, as explored by Tom Hardy's character, Eames. Inception is a very skilled art of the mind - there must be several people involved for it to be a successful job. Cobb and Arthur (Levitt's character) are the extractors/planters of the idea. Cobb recruits a skilled dream architect to design the layout of the dreams, so that they can access the person's mind with knowledge of places to go - Ariadne, (Ellen Page's Character) is the Architect. Eames is the Identity Thief and forger - he can shape-shift into other humans, and is one of the most clever and sly people in the team. According to Eames, Inception is a very subtle art - letting the idea begin just as a seed and then flowering to possible something that can change the route of their life, and define who they are. They require the heir of major corporation to dissolve his fathers empire. Creating and perceiving is what the mind does without it actually knowing - and because the mind is unaware of this process, that allows the extractors to get straight through to their mind and control. Yusuf, is a chemical compound creator - he creates sedatives for the others to become in such a deep sleep that they won't wake up without a "kick". This is where the body is pushed or made to fall backwards, in which they will wake up straight away if they already haven't been killed in the dream - in which they will also wake up. For Eames to transform into a person, he first has to know mostly every single thing about them. And for Inception to work, they must first find out the relationship between the father and son in the empire. They must study everything, because if they get one aspect, just a tiny part of the job wrong, it could mess everything up. Everything has to be on target, and synchronized. Inception is also best achieved the deeper you go into a dream state. So with his task, the sedative that Yusuf has made must enable them to delve into at least 4 layers of a dream state. The one thing that could mess everything up is Cobb's wife, Mal, who i explained about earlier. Whatever dream he is in, if he knows the layout, then his sub-conscious who projects Mal into the dreams is then able to sabotage everything. So he must not know the layout of each level of the dream. "I Will Split Up My Father's Empire" is the main idea. Each level, they have to plant a filtered version of the idea, which gets stronger on each level. At the bottom level, they bring out the "big guns", according to Eames. There is so much about the film and it is, quite confusing, the first time you see it. But each time you watch it after, you understand it a lot more, and everything becomes a lot more interesting and awesome. Anyone who liked any of Christopher Nolan's other films will thoroughly enjoy this. Admitted, it takes a little bit of concentration to understand and first, but it is one of my many favorite films. - Sam Shepherd (Shepz0r).

10.title: A Dream Odyssey
10.content:
I've sometimes heard Christopher Nolan been compared to Stanley Kubrick. Even though their films may not have that much in common, the two directors do have some similarities. As Kubrick did, Christopher Nolan also handles the producing and directing, as well as developing the screenplay of the film. And as Kubrick did, Nolan also characterizes his films with original and distinctive (even ingenious) pictures. Both directors have an identifiable style of bringing their visions to the screen. I never saw a Kubrick –film I didn't like, and so far I haven't seen a Nolan –film that I haven't liked.

Inception introduces us to a world where technology exists to enter the human mind through dream invasion. Dom Cobb (Di Caprio) is a professional thief who uses this technology to steal valuable secrets from deep within the subconscious during the dream state. This ability of his has also made Cobb an international fugitive and cost him everything that's dear to him. Now he's being offered a chance to get his life back by completing one last job. But instead of stealing an idea, he needs to plant one. Cobb gathers his team of specialists in order to succeed in this operation which is called "inception" and seems to be considered something that is impossible to do.

From the beginning to the end, Inception is an extremely fascinating entirety. A story that takes place in a dream has a lot of possibilities, because in dreams practically everything is possible. This might also be a stumbling block for some film-makers as one could easily make the mistake of exaggerating with special effects or relying too much on CGI when portraying the dreams. However, this film doesn't indulge in those kinds of things as it also leaves room for interpersonal chemistry, a bit of joking and dry humor and even an elegant little love story. The film has the proper amount of action and showy special effects. Accompanied by Hans Zimmer's sturdy (and yet so beautiful) score and some very stylish cinematography (the dream scenes in the hotel are simply amazing!), the film absorbs the viewer into the dream odyssey. The story has its complexities so also stay alert and use your brains when watching Inception.

The crew has managed to pick a very charming cast. DiCaprio does his leading role nicely. Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, Ken Watanabe, Marion Cotillard, Cillian Murphy and Dileep Rao are pleasant to watch and Michael Caine brings an extra-amount of charisma to the screen. Everyone does their job well above average.

Inception is a film that I would call a classic. This film is smart, original and entertaining. For me Stanley Kubrick had all the features of a perfect film maker. And seriously, I think Christopher Nolan is showing some similar features.

10/10

10.title: This is it!

For to many years, the bulk of the movies, that were rated 7,5 and above and were declared the best movies of those years, presented one side of an ending. The main character is in 80% of the time schizophrenic and so the ending of the movie comes with a Keyzer Soze ending, or more commonly known as a TWIST. But after seeing Shutter Isalnd and Inception, I started to wonder... Is this sort of ending, portrayed in these two movies becoming the new "THE ENDING" ? I hope so. Sure, it comes with a twist, BUT... This sort of twist gives you ONLY two possible endings. Which you prefer is up to you. It is not like in Donnie Darko, where you have 287 correct endings =) it is not like The Usual Suspects, which started the so called TWISTs, where you learn at the end of the movie, that the way you interpreted the movie was wrong... This "NEW" ending keeps you hanging. An I love it. To sum up, the movie is brilliant. It portraits our subconscious in an action way?! Wow! OK, how many of you, that gave the movie a "bad rating" would come up with this idea. It shows our philosophy and psychology in a simple but complex way. It really is a work of art! The only bad thing about this movie is, the acting of Leo. Don't get me wrong... But... Have you noticed, that his acting is the same from The Departed forth?! Same expressions, same moves, same look... I hope this is just because of the roles he plays, and that he still has an ace up his sleeve for us. Anyway, the movie is simply a must-see and I predict an instant cult classic... In more ways than one! Have a nice one!

10.title: The multiple climaxes are beautiful, elegantly flashy and grand.
10.content:
I found "Inception" disappointing, but only during its first 10 minutes. Before I bought a ticket at the box-office and ordered my Sproke (that's half-Sprite, half-Coke), I've read only two reviews about it: one tore it to pieces and micro-pieces (Rex Reed), the other one was ecstatic (Richard Roeper). In my case, by the middle of the movie, let me just say that I was swept away. As the final credits ended, I concluded that this movie was, visually a landmark, and in terms of montage a masterpiece. Three months later, I still feel the same.

Surely its weakest point must be the premise that dreams could be extracted and that ideas could be planted like viruses inside dreaming subjects' brains. That's quite a stretch. The mechanics of how this is done are hazy, or probably I wasn't listening. But once I accepted it, then I was in for rewards.

First, there's a fine ensemble of actors, particularly Leonardo DiCaprio, who became more and more sympathetic as the story unfolded and who ultimately must be credited for making us Believe.

The visual concepts and their execution are mind-boggling, hallucinatory and refreshing even if I seem to have seen them before. And the special effects are nothing less than exhilarating: the spatial distortions, the sense of being neither here nor there, the extraordinary editing. Nolan's best images are M.C. Eschers in motion or an architect's nightmare. A Parisian "arrondissement" (district) folds up like a child's picture book, bodies seem to slip in and out of mirrors and there's a ghastly panorama of a city in ruins by the sea. Could that be New York?

But what places "Inception" among landmark films is its labyrinthine narrative and how they've been pieced together. There are two strands in the plot: one about dream extractor Cobb and his ghostly wife (played with neurotic intensity by Marion Cotillard), and the other one about the inception operation. The Cobb-wife strand features several brief dreams and dreams within a dream, including dream architect Ariadne's intrusions. They move back or forth in time: sequels, prequels or story movement played out in real movie time. And they're strategically embedded throughout the film.

The anchor story, the inception operation, includes three dreams within the main dream, i.e. the scion Fischer's dream. I told my friends later that the key to enjoying the movie was not to fuss about the seeming complexity and to be always asking: which dream am I watching now? But if you insist, I said, remember that those four-layered dreams move in parallel, and in logical progression. Plus, the settings tell us which dream layer we're in: the hotel corridor, the city road, the jumbo jet, somewhere in the Alps, and the river.

"Inception" hits an explosive point when each of those subplot dreams reaches its climax in breathtaking sequence. They are beautiful, elegantly flashy, and grand in a way the climaxes of classic films are. The resolution of the Cobb-wife story neatly wraps up everything. Or does it? Cobb's operative "token," a metallic top, continues its endless spin, indicating that he, and us, are still caught up in a dream.

Christopher Nolan has all the credentials to be hailed as a master of the deconstructed narrative and classical montage. I believe that it will end up not just one of the top 10 movies of the year; it will be one of the top three. The French L'Express newspaper reviewer wrote that "Inception is a cinematic miracle disguised as a Hollywood blockbuster." I couldn't agree more.

10.title: A less biased review, hopefully
10.content:
So anyway, I went to see Inception last night at the cinema. Was totally blown away.

I then came home and had a look on IMDb to see what other people thought. I found it fairly shocking that people had decided to rate this film 1/10 and other equally low ratings.

Sure, you can compare this film to Kubrick's work if you like, but how is this film anything like what he's ever done? It's not.

I think a lot of people like to think they 'know film', but really they're just sheep. Hear how they harp on about very popular 'masters of film' such as Kubrick and Hitchcock, and don't get me wrong I loved The Shining, 2001 was a bit boring really wasn't it unless you were born in the 60s seeing it on acid, rear window was cool as was south by south west.. but wait, this film had awesome action and AN AWESOME PLOT.

If you like a good story, then go see this film. If you're more interested in how well somebody is acting, what 'the director was thinking' etc.. go see something else and really have a think about why you watch films in the first place.

I was tempted to give this a 10/10 to offset the stupid hateful reviews a bit but I resisted. I also started thinking about how IMDb should re- think it's rating system. I think the rating of a film should also take into consideration it's release date as a weighting to the total average.

Anyway, if you have an open mind, go see this film!

10.title: Dynamite Inception go see it with lessend expectations maybe twice
10.content: Christopher Nolan gave us the 2001 indie breakthrough Memento. Supposedly he spent 10 years writing this screenplay/plot for this dreamscape movie. (KIND OF A Matrix 2010)In this new film director tosses off more ideas & plot devices most blockbusters would never had the nerve to attempt. Dom Cobb is a skilled thief, the absolute best in the dangerous art of extraction, stealing valuable secrets from deep within the subconscious during the dream state, when the mind is at its most vulnerable. Cobb's rare ability has made him a coveted player in this treacherous new world of corporate espionage, but it has also made him an international fugitive & cost him everything he has ever loved. Now Cobb is being offered a chance at redemption. One last job could give him his life back but only if he can accomplish the impossible-inception. Instead of the perfect heist, Cobb & his team of specialists have to pull off the reverse: their task is not to steal an idea but to plant one. If they succeed, it could be the perfect crime. But no amount of careful planning or expertise can prepare the team for the dangerous enemy that seems to predict their every move. An enemy that only Cobb could have seen coming. Christopher Nolan is one of Hollywood's most inventive dreamers/directors. Inception Is very clever. Concentrating on the procedural details of mind crime this is a devilishly intricate yarn set in the layers of the subconscious. Nolan gives a heist thriller for the surreal. That challenges film goers to unravel & understand multiple layers of (un)reality. Film has exceptional cinematography set designs & special effects. Film give a simulation of fake reality intended to seduce us, mess up our heads & leave a lasting impression. Film is a success but much of the time viewers are lost & disoriented. In the age of remakes & sequels & franchises. Inception does a difficult thing—it is completely & uniquely original. Highest rating you might need to see this movie twice
