10.title: Artistic, thought-provoking, and original. I can't ask for more.
10.content:
My number one reason for liking Inception might seem fanboyish, but I'll say it anyway: it's a Christopher Nolan film.

Now, my reasons for liking Nolan's films are too numerous to count, but I'll say this: he is one of the very few directors who makes artistic, thoughtful films on a blockbuster budget. Starting out as an indie director with Memento, Nolan really hit his stride when he inherited the Batman franchise and made his Dark Knight trilogy (which I will cover later in this series). However, he always had a knack for taking original content such as the magician-focused novel The Prestige or creating his own original ideas.

This is where Inception comes in. How many films can you say have been made about the subconscious of the human mind? And how many of those got the budget of Inception? Nolan is ambitious, I'll give him that. Thankfully, he uses his ambition and passion together, making what seems as one pet project after another. His devotion to his craft is rare in today's industry. Inception evidences this beautifully: Nolan wrote his own script and, as is typical for his films, never allowed second unit filming, directing every single shot himself. He is also very particular about his effects, opting for practical, real stunts and visuals instead of generating them on a computer. Inception has less CG shots than even Batman Begins, which is quite obviously mostly real in its effects. This grounds his films in reality and makes them more fun to watch.

Speaking of visuals, let's talk about Inception's aesthetic. Most of Nolan's films are worked on by cinematographer Wally Pfister, and while he has done excellent work in all of his Nolan collaborations, this is his best. The way he changes the color palette through each layer of the dream is quite subtle but very effective, helping us keep track of where we are throughout the complicated climax. Other scenes, particularly in the lowest dream level, show us an excellent knowledge of scale and scope on Pfister's part. The best parts, however, are when he uses high-speed cameras to slow down the film to reflect the time changes between the levels. It ties everything together beautifully and helps us understand how that process works.

That moves us right on to the best aspect of Inception: the story. I can't really go into detail here without spoilers because this is one of the more complex plots I've ever seen. Just know this: repeat viewings are almost required. This is not for comprehension, but rather to pick up on all the nuances that are here. There is so much to this plot that I am still picking up nuances upon watching Inception for the ninth time and enjoying the film even more. In case you can't tell, this is not a movie where you can turn your brain off and slip mindlessly into another world. You have to pay attention or you will lose track of what's happening.

To keep this short, I'll say only one thing about the score and then move on: Hans Zimmer is the best film composer today. This film gave him that title.

Inception's cast is almost as big as I've seen in any film. Leonardo DiCaprio is the top-billed star, but that is incredibly misleading as this film is a true ensemble piece. He also doesn't steal the show in Inception like he usually does, leaving others a lot of room to work. The one thing that is starting to get to me about DiCaprio is that, as good as he is, all of his characters seem the same. They all struggle with their inner demons extensively throughout the course of the film, and Cobb is no different. Outside of DiCaprio, the acting is equally stellar, with Tom Hardy and Cillian Murphy stealing the show. Hardy plays Eames, a forger for Cobb's job who is one of the very few characters with any kind of comic relief. He really shows his range here and proves that he can help carry a film. Murphy plays the subject of the final job, Robert Fischer. I feel that he best embodies how we react to ideas in our subconscious and really made Inception relatable to the audience.

Inception is a masterpiece, and an original one at that, from the man responsible for some of the best films of this century to date. Christopher Nolan really knows how to bring all the elements of a film together into one coherent vision, from the story to the casting to the aesthetic to the score. Every part of this film contributes to the overall vision. Inception is one of my favorite films because it challenges the mind and makes it think. In a world of escapist entertainment, this film makes us explore our minds and our ideas in a way I've never seen before.

10.title: Explore the subconscious within a dream... and within that dream dreaming.
10.content:
Let's create a multi-leveled dream where we can extract ideas off our enemies or implant an idea bypassing memories and consciousness: groundbreaking, original, complex, cerebral, psychological, systemic, and astute. The descriptors are insufficient to bring justice to this tremendously brilliant endeavor. The dialogue also presents obscure ideas that have rarely been explored in movies, or at least that I have not seen. At the onset the mystical dialogue attempts to explain the nature of the extraction, and, as the scenes take place, the viewer gets tempted by the explanation of worlds created by an architect where subjects can get robbed from their ideas or implanted in the case of the major heist of the movie.

Simply following and understanding the complex setting and the intricacies of the implanting is a challenge. The movie navigates a fast pace and is able to explain the complex events of the movie in a surprisingly effective style. Christopher Nolan presents the essential details in snippets of interactions that bring a lively and charismatic depiction to the process of learning about the heist. We also enjoy a diverse cast that amalgamates to deliver us an interesting exploration of Cobb's (Leonardo Dicaprio) perception. Ariadne (Ellen Page) is presented as a gifted college student that is extraordinarily apt at building mazes. She progressively gets to know more about the heist and Cobb's projections manifested in her mazes and, despite her repeatedly expressing her concern; we can't help but feel her emotions of compassion, sadness, and empathy. If Cobb was to show her the depths of his unconscious, the cast needed a sensitive rendition like the one displayed by Ariadne. Arthur is also, from the first scenes, supporting Cobb despite knowing all the baggage and the risks he implicates. Even despite Arthur risking everyone's life, the group still continues with the mission and finishes in dramatic fashion.

There are so many levels at which inception can be analyzed, but what is at the pinnacle of the experience for me is the innovation and dialogue. Movies as innovative and cerebral like inception should be celebrated and rewarded for their brilliant effort.

10.title: The movie is all about process, about fighting our way through enveloping sheets of reality and dream, reality within dreams, dreams without reality
10.content:
The story can either be told in a few sentences, or not told at all. Here is a movie immune to spoilers: If you knew how it ended, that would tell you nothing unless you knew how it got there. And telling you how it got there would produce bafflement. The movie is all about process, about fighting our way through enveloping sheets of reality and dream, reality within dreams, dreams without reality. It's a breathtaking juggling act, and Nolan may have considered his "Memento" (2000) a warm-up; he apparently started this screenplay while filming that one. It was the story of a man with short-term memory loss, and the story was told backwards.

Like the hero of that film, the viewer of "Inception" is adrift in time and experience. We can never even be quite sure what the relationship between dream time and real time is. The hero explains that you can never remember the beginning of a dream, and that dreams that seem to cover hours may only last a short time. Yes, but you don't know that when you're dreaming. And what if you're inside another man's dream? How does your dream time synch with his? What do you really know?

10.title: I cannot recommend this film anymore than I have, I just have to say everyone and anyone should see it. Sorry about all the gushing, it is just so hard not too...
10.content:
Usually I try to be careful with over hyping a film, or setting the expectations too high, as film geeks all are guilty for, however for Christopher Nolan's Inception, this really is not possible.

This is possibly one of the only perfect films I have ever seen. It is absolutely confident in every way, something which is extremely refreshing, even more so than Avatar. Christopher Nolan gets some slack for making great to look at but ultimately heartless affairs, which I for one do not agree with, however I do not think anyone can argue that here. The emotional aspect of this film not only ties it all together but is really the center of this film, it is the focus.

I do not want to over simplify the film, by simply calling it Kubrick doing Bond, or Gondry on a huge budget, because I am sure it will be called that but it is far more than that, it is something I do not think Kubrick could have ever made. It is pure Nolan, and pure greatness.

I hate writing something which is pure fan-boy gushing, but its really difficult here. I did not find a thing I did not like about it, I am sure if maybe I saw it a second time, maybe I would find something about it I didn't like, but not the first time. The way it is cut, means that there is always action on screen, if not, then the visuals are interesting enough to keep your eyes glued.

The final hour of the film, is possibly one of the most complicated action sequences put on film. You have to constantly be paying attention to remember all of the layers of what is happening. Without spoiling anything, all I have to say is that is what this film is about, that is what makes this film so great, layers. Once you have seen this you will now what I am talking about.

All of the actors are fantastic too, Di Caprio is the stand out here. Yes, this is probably due to the fact he is the star and given all of the emotional weight, but he handles it perfectly, similarly to his performance in Shutter Island. Ellen Page, whom I usually hate, gives a great performance here. Tom Hardy gives a break out performance here, he is quite the bad ass.

I hope audiences are ready for a film like this, a pure auteur driven film which does not sacrifice a single frame for the studio. I would hope this film will change Hollywood, as it is 100 percent the directors vision yet it is definitely a marketable film, much like District 9, yet I do not think it will.

10.title: "Inception": A Mind-Bending Masterpiece of Modern Cinema
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" is a tour de force of imagination and storytelling, a mind-bending journey into the depths of the subconscious that captivates and mesmerizes from start to finish. With its dazzling visuals, intricate plot, and profound thematic depth, this film stands as a testament to Nolan's unparalleled skill as a filmmaker and storyteller.

At the heart of "Inception" is a concept both simple and profound: the ability to enter and manipulate dreams. Led by the charismatic Leonardo DiCaprio as Dom Cobb, a skilled extractor tasked with planting an idea in the mind of a wealthy businessman, the film follows Cobb and his team as they navigate the treacherous terrain of the human mind, encountering danger, deception, and unexpected revelations along the way.

What sets "Inception" apart from other films in the sci-fi genre is its rich thematic tapestry. Nolan weaves together elements of reality, memory, and perception to create a narrative that is as intellectually stimulating as it is emotionally resonant. The film explores profound questions about the nature of reality, the power of dreams, and the nature of guilt and redemption, inviting audiences to ponder the nature of their own existence and the choices that shape their lives.

Of course, "Inception" is also a technical marvel, with groundbreaking visual effects and breathtaking action sequences that push the boundaries of what is possible on screen. From the gravity-defying antics of the zero-gravity hotel fight to the mind-bending architecture of dreamscapes within dreamscapes, every frame is a testament to Nolan's unparalleled vision and ambition.

But perhaps the greatest achievement of "Inception" is its emotional depth and resonance. At its core, the film is a deeply human story, exploring themes of loss, regret, and the search for redemption. DiCaprio delivers a powerhouse performance as Cobb, capturing the character's inner turmoil and existential angst with a raw intensity and vulnerability that is truly captivating.

In conclusion, "Inception" is a masterpiece of modern cinema-a film that challenges, provokes, and ultimately inspires with its dazzling visuals, intricate plot, and profound thematic depth. Whether you're drawn in by its mind-bending premise or its rich emotional storytelling, one thing is certain: "Inception" is a cinematic experience unlike any other, a timeless classic that continues to captivate and enthrall audiences with each passing viewing.

10.title: Worth watching
10.content:
_Inception: A Mind-Bending Masterpiece of Cinematic Storytelling_

Christopher Nolan's "Inception" (2010) is a thought-provoking and visually stunning sci-fi action film that delves into the complexities of the human mind. This critically acclaimed movie is a game-changer in the world of cinema, redefining the boundaries of storytelling and pushing the limits of visual effects. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and pulse-pounding action sequences, "Inception" is a must-see for film enthusiasts and anyone looking for a cinematic experience that will leave them breathless.

The movie follows Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), a skilled thief who specializes in entering people's dreams and stealing their secrets. Cobb is hired by a wealthy businessman named Saito (Ken Watanabe) to perform a task known as "inception" - planting an idea in someone's mind instead of stealing one. Saito wants Cobb to convince Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy), the son of a dying business magnate, to dissolve his father's company. In return, Saito promises to clear Cobb's name, which is wanted by the authorities, and allow him to return to the United States to see his children.

Cobb assembles a team of experts, including Arthur (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), Ariadne (Ellen Page), Eames (Tom Hardy), and Saito, to help him perform the inception. As they delve deeper into Fischer's dreams, the team faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including projections of their own subconscious and the blurred lines between reality and dreams.

One of the standout aspects of "Inception" is its complex and layered storyline. Nolan's script is a masterclass in storytelling, weaving together multiple plot threads and timelines with ease. The film's use of non-linear storytelling adds to the complexity, keeping the viewer on the edge of their seat as they try to piece together the puzzle.

The cast delivers outstanding performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. DiCaprio shines as Cobb, a character haunted by his past and struggling to come to terms with his reality. The supporting cast, including Gordon-Levitt, Page, and Hardy, add to the film's emotional impact with their portrayals of Cobb's team.

The film's visuals are simply stunning, with Nolan pushing the boundaries of what is possible on screen. The action sequences are intense and thrilling, with the hotel corridor fight scene being a particular highlight. The special effects are seamless, creating a dream world that is both believable and visually stunning.

The themes of "Inception" are thought-provoking and timely, exploring the nature of reality, the power of the human mind, and the consequences of playing with fire. The film raises questions about the stability of our perceptions and the ease with which they can be manipulated.

In conclusion, "Inception" is a mind-bending masterpiece of cinematic storytelling that is not to be missed. With its complex and layered storyline, outstanding performances, and stunning visuals, this film is a must-see for anyone looking for a cinematic experience that will challenge their perceptions and leave them breathless. If you haven't seen "Inception" before, do yourself a favor and watch it - but be prepared for.

10.title: Masterpiece
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" is a mind-bending masterpiece that defies the conventions of traditional storytelling. The film follows Dom Cobb, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, as he navigates the intricate world of corporate espionage through the manipulation of dreams. As Cobb and his team delve deeper into the subconscious, the lines between reality and illusion blur, leading to an exhilarating journey through the layers of the mind.

Nolan's direction is nothing short of visionary, seamlessly weaving together a complex narrative with stunning visual effects and a haunting score by Hans Zimmer. The film's concept of dream infiltration opens the door to a myriad of possibilities, allowing for breathtaking action sequences and mind-bending twists that keep audiences guessing until the very end.

DiCaprio delivers a captivating performance as Cobb, a troubled protagonist haunted by his past and driven by his desire to reunite with his family. His emotional journey serves as the heart of the film, grounding the fantastical elements in a deeply human story of redemption and forgiveness.

The supporting cast, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, and Tom Hardy, each bring their own unique talents to the table, adding depth and dimension to the ensemble. Their chemistry and camaraderie elevate the film beyond its high-concept premise, creating characters that are both relatable and compelling.

"Inception" is a cinematic experience unlike any other, challenging viewers to question the nature of reality and the power of the subconscious mind. It is a testament to Nolan's unparalleled skill as a filmmaker, pushing the boundaries of storytelling while delivering a thrilling and thought-provoking ride from start to finish. With its jaw-dropping visuals, innovative premise, and emotional depth, "Inception" stands as a modern classic that continues to captivate audiences years after its release.

10.title: Why I love this movie so much?
10.content:
It is one of the most open to interpretation movies that I ever seen. Every time I watch it there's a new perspective to consider. For example there are arguments to be made that the whole movie is a dream. There is the obvious analogy between the cast and a movie crew. Then there is the soundtrack that is basically made after portions of the music "Non je ne regrette rien" by Edit Piaf that are either speeded up or slowed down. Not to mention the movie's lenght which is 2 hours and 28 minutes, while the song from Edit Piaf is 2 minutes and 28 seconds.


The movie's ending is a red hearing, because the totem is basically a distraction for the audience, just like the story of The Prestige is a distraction for the audience to not see the obvious trick in the movie which is later revealed by the end of the movie. For example any other totems behave specially in the real world but ordinary in the dream world. While Cobb's behaves normally in the real world and specially in the dream. But someone who would create a dream and not knowing that would apply the rule that the spin wouldfall not go on forever. That means that he could be in anyone's dream by the end. Why the end is so powerful and satisfying is because he accepts his family and stops trying to do any other dream heists or worrying about the fact that he might be dreaming or not.


The movie's characters are all one-sided, aside from Cobb. That is another indication that all of them might be projections in Cobb's dream, which is actually the movie itself. It's so mind-blowing that the more you dwell in the film and rewatch it the more you discover small things and new possibilities for interpretation.


It's an allegory that life might be just a simulation and that nothing is real. How do we prove life is real? I'm telling you, you can't... so you just choose to believe that on faith alone? No proof? These are questions the movie raises.


I could go on and talking about all the things I love about this movie, but that would make the review almost impossible to be read because it would be too long. This is a masterpiece that won't be equalled by almost anything else. Comparing this movie to Matrix makes me puke. That movie is just a bad joke about intellectual concepts, that has neither the logic nor the storytelling potential to fully realize it's intellectual concepts. 10/10

10.title: The Definition of a Perfect Summer Blockbuster!
10.content:
So before Inception, Christopher Nolan made Doodlebug, Following, Memento, Insomnia, Batman Begins, The Prestige, The Dark Knight. And looking at that kind of filmography, there can be no way that this movie is bad.

Inception is one of the best movies I have ever seen in my entire life! This is one of the reasons why I love movies and it exceeded my expectations! Modern Filmmakers should learn from this movie!

The Acting in this movie is flawless, we have an all-star cast staring Leonardo DiCaprio, Ken Watanabe, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Marion Cotillard, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, Cillian Murphy, Tom Berenger, and Michael Caine. Leonardo DiCaprio gives the audience another great performance as always and I still can't believe that he hasn't won an Oscar yet! Joseph Gordon-Levitt is a great actor, he was good in "(500) Days of Summer" but in this movie, he shows that he can play a different character pull it off perfectly! Tom Hardy (before playing Bane) was excellent, he fit his role perfectly. Michael Caine has a brief role in this movie and I don't even have to tell you he's good because no matter what he's in, he's never bad.

The Writing is intelligent, this is one of the most original stories I have ever seen in my entire life. It's 100% original that you don't even know what will happen in the next scene and the story takes us into directions we didn't expect and that brings the quality of the film higher.

Hans Zimmer's score in this movie is fantastic, not only is this movie original but also the score is, and this is my favorite score from him!

The effects are astounding, they looked so realistic that my jaw dropped many times! Some scenes where effects are used and it has to do with a building, it looks like it was a real scale but it was a set and that is so mind blowing about the effects in Christopher Nolan's movies, he uses practical effects over CGI.

This movie is a blockbuster but not in a way where it's a mindless blockbuster. It's a smart, thought-provoking, perfectly paced blockbuster film and another thing I love about Christopher Nolan's movies is that he always gives us something new and his movies aren't just for mindless entertainment, you have to pay attention and think when you're watching the movie.

I rarely leave the theater satisfied nowadays and it seems like the only Director that satisfies me is Christopher Nolan: he is intelligent, hard-working, reliable, and consistent.

I could not have asked for a better movie, Inception is Christopher Nolan's Masterpiece!

When Saito (Ken Wantanabe) gives Cobb the task of inception (the art of planting an idea through their mind) he also offers Cobb the chance to see his children again. He accepts and Cobb and his team are given the task of planting the idea inside the mind of CEO Robert Fischer (Cillian Murphy). Cobb and his team isolate Fischer on a plane and though a series of dreams give him the idea that Saito wanted him to have. The music by Hans Zimmer is amazing. Nolan's plot, his trickiest since Memento, is such that the second you overtake it, things start to fray – so he isn't about to let that happen in a hurry.

Leonardo DiCaprio, in a frazzled and unhelpfully humorless performance, gives the impression he never got the boat off Shutter Island. The concept is cool and all, but think about how dreams really function for a second, and it teeters on the brink of wrongheadedness. Don't we dream of sex, at all? 10.title: A Rare Film
10.content:
Story: What stands out most in "Inception" is its originality, particularly in its non-linear storytelling, which is a characteristic feature of Nolan's movies. The movie has a complex narrative, with layers of dreams that unfold in a mind-bending manner. It's initially confusing but brilliantly executed.

Visual Storytelling: I am impressed with such clever details of how actors who are in the dream are checked whether they are really in the dream. There are very cool unexpected moments in the dream sequences that showcase the film's capacity to surprise and impress viewers. The special effects are impressive, highlighting advanced physics and carefully crafted real-life 3D models.

Cinematography: Inception (2010) shines with its crisp cinematography, using medium and close-up shots and slow zoom-ins building tension. The chase scene set in Mombasa is a visual treat, showcasing the film's thoughtful location choices. The stunts, though appearing dangerous, are impressively executed and add a rare quality to the movie. The film's slow motion sequences are truly remarkable. It beautifully captures the idea of a dream within a dream in a thorough manner and showcasing Christopher Nolan's brilliance.

Music: Hans Zimmer's score is nothing short of amazing, elevating the film's immersive experience, especially notable in the Dolby Atmos format that I watched this film. Zimmer's use of drums and stutter effects adds to the film's dynamic pace.

Actors and Acting: Leonardo DiCaprio's (as Mr. Cobb) performance is exceptional, bringing depth to his character. DiCaprio's acting, combined with rapid camera movements, intensifies the drama surrounding Cillian Murphy's (as Robert Fischer) character. Mal, who was played by Marion Cotillard, had a callous character with a very specific accent. It did not resonate with me personally, yet, her role fits very well within the film's narrative.

In conclusion, "Inception" is a cinematic masterpiece. It's a movie that not only entertains but also challenges and captivates its audience.

10.title: Inception: A Cinematic Masterpiece of Mind-Bending Complexity, Earns a Perfect 10 with an Ending That Sparks Endless Dreams and Debates.

Visually, it's a feast, with the zero-gravity hallway scene still blowing my mind. And let's talk about that ending - I'm all in on it being a dream. The spinning top, the uncertainty, it's like Nolan's way of messing with our heads, keeping the debate alive. Sure, it demands some brainpower to keep up, but that's part of the fun. A 10/10 because it's a cinematic masterpiece that challenges your perception, leaving you with more questions than answers, and that's the beauty of it.

10.title: Absolutely Perfectly Brilliant!!!
10.content:
My goodness me is this a fantastically terrific movie!! I watched this movie in August and here I am now in November and I am still in awe of it! Christopher Nolan has delivered yet anther mesmerizing masterpiece and while I can write pages and pages of it, I realize this is a complex movie with many long reviews so I will try and keep this short...ish.

Inception tells the the story of Cobb (DiCaprio) who along with his team builds dreams. They then place their subject into that dream and allow them to "fill it with their secrets". That's about as simply as I can explain it because you can imagine that once that dream is filled, the manipulation Cobb can do is endless. Cobb gets enlisted to perform 'inception' on a high profile figure i.e: place an idea into the subject through placing them in a dream you created for them. The movie basically follows the protagonists in their mission all the while showing Cobb try to deal with the trauma in his life. That's all say about the storyline as I don't want to give too much away.

The positive points for this movie are endless. Firstly, the acting! Leonardo DiCaprio has matured into IMO the finest actor of his generation and his performance in Inception is truly outstanding, riveting, emotional, deep and definitely for me deserves the Best Actor Oscar! The rest of the cast pull in equally terrific performances which makes this one of the best acted films I have seen (and I have watched all the legends at their peak!). Secondly, the effects are jaw-dropping. Forget the Matrix "rip-offs" and what other nonsense the few negative reviews claim; the effects will leave you spellbound and completely make this movie a masterpiece. Thirdly, Hans Zimmer pulls in with a terrific score which captures the feel of the movie incredibly well and masterfully aids in building emotion where needed. Fourthly, the storyline is absolutely original and perfectly woven and told! Make no mistake, this is a complex movie with complex themes but with a fair bit of concentration, you will absolutely love it! I could go on and on...and so I shall; fifthly, the ending is utterly brilliant and will leave you reeling and thinking long after this movie ends (as it did with me!).

I have long waited for a movie of such high caliber and this blew my expectations right out the door and set new ones at a stratospheric level! If this movie does not get Best Picture, Best Screenplay, Best Director and Best Actor in the next Oscars, I will completely denounce the Oscars as a hoax! This movie is still playing in some theaters so I beg you, do yourself a favor and go see this; a movie which will definitely live to earn legendary status. All the hype is in fact underrated and you will not be disappointed no matter how high your expectations are! If there was a score of more than 10/10, I would give it. My only wish is that Nolan never stops making movies!

P.S. If you want to see a really good trailer of it, check out Inception Trailer 2 on youtube!

10.title: The Most Brilliant Movie Ever Made
10.content: Quite simply, I believe that this film, Inception, with Christopher Nolan at the helm, is the greatest film ever made. Each scene is directed with pure, exciting, cinematic power that grips and envelops the audience with suspense, thrills, and fun. The script is admittedly hard to understand with your first watch, but, as you understand, realize, and take time to think deeply about each aspect, then let the film explain the rest, watching Inception might be the best movie experience of your lifetime. Every tiny plot twist, which shall not be given away here, keeps you interested and has a fresh, innovative, and brazenly original touch. The feel and the form of the film has never been seen before, and it seems to tease other movies that are lazy with their efforts to improve the quality of the film, and use their massive budgets to produce special effects that attract brain-dead explosion junkies to the box office like a moth to a light. As many have realized, the reason that Inception is the greatest film effort ever organized, is that Christopher Nolan, writer, director, and producer of this film, works his hardest to make his audience happy. If you think too hard about this movie, you're missing the point. Christopher Nolan does not want to confuse you, he wants you to have more fun than other shallow movies that are only a good watch the first time around. He gives the film its literally multi-layered function so that you can watch it twenty times and still find new details that make you love it even more. I have watched this movie around 25 times and I am still discovering new things with every experience. People all around the globe are realizing that Christopher Nolan, maybe the best filmmaker that has ever lived, treats his audience like he would want to feel when watching a movie. Important. Smart. Able to understand/handle anything that happens on screen, and most important of all, to have a blast. This movie is a shining example of the love that he puts into his work, and how we should cherish a beautiful and life-changing film like this by watching it, enjoying it, and not criticizing the confusing nature because we do not understand it, but be thankful that a man who respects his customers as much as, and maybe more, than the average, everyday, working man, makes a film for those of us who do. I hope you enjoy Inception as much I have, and I hope you learn more about Christopher Nolan, one of the most under-appreciated and misunderstood entertainers of the modern world.

10.title: Incredible Movie!
10.content:
"Inception" stands as a true cinematic marvel, a product of Christopher Nolan's visionary mind. Amidst the flood of reboots, remakes, and sequels, Nolan's blend of drama and grandeur sets "Inception" apart as a genuine original during blockbuster season.

Attempting to dissect the myriad plot twists and intricacies of "Inception" would be a futile endeavor, as Nolan himself has been reticent to do so. The best approach to the film is with an open mind, ready to embark on a journey unlike any other. If "Avatar" was groundbreaking in its technological advancements (though lacking in narrative, in my personal opinion), then "Inception" achieves a similar milestone in storytelling. Despite its 148-minute runtime, the film's pacing is relentless, never allowing a moment of boredom to creep in. Each aspect of the film is imbued with depth, leaving the viewer spellbound throughout.

While the storytelling prowess of "Inception" may dominate discussions, the spectacle is equally astounding. The action sequences, as hinted in the trailer, are breathtakingly real yet unbelievably surreal. Unlike typical blockbusters, these set pieces serve to enhance the narrative rather than merely satisfy a desire for explosions, a testament to Nolan's directorial finesse.

A film of such complexity demands a stellar cast, and Nolan delivers just that. Leonardo DiCaprio delivers a performance reminiscent of his work in "The Aviator," anchoring the film with his portrayal of Cobb. Despite the character's subdued nature, DiCaprio expertly navigates Cobb's emotional complexities. The supporting cast shines as well, with Cillian Murphy displaying unexpected tenderness, Joseph Gordon-Levitt exuding confidence as Arthur, Ken Watanabe portraying ambiguity with devilish charm, Ellen Page showcasing her rising star power, and Tom Hardy providing comic relief in contrast to his recent menacing roles.

Overall, Nolan has outdone himself with "Inception." He has crafted a world as expansive as Gotham, a plot more intricate than "Memento," and a cinematic reveal that eclipses "The Prestige." This is essential viewing, a masterpiece to be savored as we anxiously await the next installment of Nolan's Batman saga.

10.title: A Masterful Blend of Intellectual Depth and Cinematic Excellence
10.content:
"Inception," directed by the visionary Christopher Nolan, is an extraordinary cinematic achievement that redefines the boundaries of storytelling. This film is not just a movie; it's an intricate labyrinth of ideas, emotions, and breathtaking visuals that pulls you into its depths from the first frame to the last.

Leonardo DiCaprio delivers a powerful performance as Dom Cobb, a skilled thief who infiltrates the subconscious of his targets. DiCaprio masterfully portrays Cobb's internal battle, balancing his professional prowess with his haunted past. The supporting cast, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, and Marion Cotillard, are equally compelling, each adding depth and intrigue to the narrative.

The concept of the film is its most striking aspect. Nolan introduces the idea of dream extraction and inception with such finesse that it seems both fantastical and plausible. The story unfolds like a Russian nesting doll, with layers within layers, each more intricate than the last. This complexity is not just for show; it forms the backbone of the film's exploration of themes like perception, reality, and personal catharsis.

The visual effects in "Inception" are nothing short of groundbreaking. From the Paris dreamscape bending in on itself to the zero-gravity hallway fight, each scene is a marvel of cinematic artistry. The special effects serve the story, enhancing the surreal quality of the dream world while maintaining a sense of visceral reality.

Hans Zimmer's score is another element that elevates "Inception." The music is both haunting and beautiful, perfectly complementing the film's tone and enhancing the emotional impact of key scenes. The use of the slowed-down version of Edith Piaf's "Non, Je Ne Regrette Rien" is particularly ingenious, intertwining with the plot in a way that is both clever and impactful.

What truly sets "Inception" apart is its ability to challenge the viewer intellectually while providing a thrilling, emotionally resonant story. It's a film that invites analysis and discussion, offering new insights with each viewing. The ending, which has sparked much debate, is a stroke of genius, leaving the audience questioning the nature of reality and the power of the human mind.

In conclusion, "Inception" is more than just a movie; it's an experience that pushes the boundaries of what cinema can achieve. It's a rare gem that combines intellectual depth with sheer entertainment value. For its innovative storytelling, stunning visuals, exceptional performances, and profound thematic exploration, "Inception" deserves nothing less than a perfect 10 out of 10.

10.title: One of the Greatest movies of the 21st Century
10.content:
If I were to make a list of my favourite movies of all time, this one has got to be in the top five. As is usual with Christopher Nolan movies, Inception blew my mind.

Just like in every Nolan movie, it takes effort to make it make sense. In the film, the complexity of the dream world, if understood, does make it even more interesting. Nolan does this through scenes that heavily rely on dialogue.

Inception might be an action movie, but, just like The Dark Knight Trilogy, it's so much more than that. It's a psychological thriller of the highest calibre. It's packed with riddles and concepts but the plot also relies heavily on the emotional vulnerability of its characters. The actors pulled off their roles so seamlessly that it's as if the characters were written for them, especially Leo DiCaprio.

Nolan manages to weave parallel plots together with little, if any, room for plot holes, and leave the rest up for interpretation. The pieces of the Inception puzzle do fit perfectly in the end. They're intentionally left out, so the viewers could put them together and see the bigger picture for themselves.

10.title: "Inception" - Navigating the Labyrinth of Reality and Dreams
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" delves into the intricate landscape where our reliance on computerized technology and manipulated media shapes our perceptions and holds us hostage from the sensations we consider our own. Much like the protagonist Dominick "Dom" Cobb, who, in a dream, implants an idea into another's mind, the film questions the concept of free thought in a society that dictates meaning and conformity.

The film plays with the ambiguous boundaries between reality and dreams, reminiscent of the quote, "dreams, they feel real while we're in them, right?" (Inception, 2010). Nolan's deliberate inconsistencies and symbolic elements keep the audience navigating a maze of images and simulations. The theatricality of the film, from its intricate dream scenarios to the narrowing and widening maze of the protagonist's logical world, challenges our perception of reality.

Key moments in "Inception" resonate with the song "Dream is Collapsing," aligning the film's narrative with the track's duration. The audience is taken on a journey into the protagonist's dreams, blurring the lines between deliberate dreams and waking life. The uncertainty surrounding the spinning top in the film's ending leaves viewers questioning the reliability of Dominick's account, adding layers of ambiguity and overdramatization.

Christopher Nolan intentionally crafts a film that transcends the conventional, weaving a narrative that explores the depths of the mind and challenges our understanding of reality. "Inception" is a cinematic labyrinth, inviting audiences to question the fine line between dreams and the tangible, leaving us to ponder whether the film's enigmatic totality was ever intended to be confirmed. #Inception #RealityVsDreams #ChristopherNolanMagic.

10.title: Simply a blockbuster!!!!

'Inception' is considered one of DiCaprio's best movies ever. It reveals in a unique yet very simple way, how deep a human's mind is. Drowning into someone's mind and planting an idea inside it, and also making it looks like it was his all time along, that's the plot of the movie in a few words. But what can't be summarized in a few words or even pages is the emotional condition that overwhelmed me while watching that movie in the cinema for the first time. Over two hours of excitement, action, comedy and the sweet love story between Cobb and Mal, that story that was the base of the movie's events.

Though the movie didn't introduce backgrounds for any of the characters, except for Cobb, which left us wondering about the past of Arthur, Eames, and maybe Ariadne, you never feel that the movie is imperfect in anyway. On the contrary, you will -deliciously- fall in love with every character. You will feel sorry for Cobb, you will like Eames's sense of humor and Arthur's mysterious looks and gentleness. Even Saito the business-man has his own nice moments as well.

I think that although the movie is "action-fantasy" movie, but it's a romance movie in the first place. The scenes of Cobb and his beautiful wife, Mal, and their life together in limbo that lasted for over fifty years proves so. They sacrificed a lot of things just to be together as long as life can allow them.

Finally, 'Inception' is definitely one of the movies I will never forget. I can watch it everyday without getting bored. It's just perfect....in every way.

10.title: Christopher Nolan has created a masterpiece
10.content: SPOILERS! The name Christopher Nolan has become synonymous with amazing Hollywood films in recent years. They see him as a man who can simply direct a movie that will entertain the masses. However, few truly understand his genius. On the contrary, Christopher Nolan knows how to portray abstract ideas on the big screen better than anyone. For the truth is that there are plenty of directors who can make an engaging movie that people will like. Christopher Nolan presents abstract ideas about dreams in the the movie "Inception" using beautiful cinematography and clear plot devices such as timing and layering that keep the audience engaged and thinking. I think Inception is a great film for a few reasons: the cinematography is amazing, the cast is stellar, it is action packed, and it visualized abstract ideas. The cinematography captures the amazing settings such as that of the street of Paris, France and the beautiful arctic mountains of Kananaskis Canada. Christopher Nolan also took the time to shoot scenes using practical effects rather than using CGI. This makes the movie seem more realistic and interesting. He builds set with impossible shapes like the Penrose Steps and a stairwell loop. Using camera tricks and editing he is able to make the impossible look possible. Movie that rely on CGI rather practical effects provide a more realistic feel to a film that CGI, in all its 21st century glory, can't do justice. The cast of Inception is a recipe for success. The cast consists of only the best actors that have a history for making good movies. Leonardo DiCaprio the main protagonist has been in good films since he was like 15 years old when he was in "What's Eating Gilbert Grape" with Johnny Depp. Other consistently successful actors such as Joseph Gordan-Levvit, Ellen Page, and Tom Hardy play supporting characters throughout the film. The chemistry between them on top of the skillful acting results in a realistic movie that engulfs you into the plot of the movie. The movie also has a lot of action in it. Inception is essentially a heist movie, but they are planting something in someone's mind instead of trying to steal something. There are guns, goons, car chases, and explosions. A recipe for any good action movie. The action in the plot keeps the story interesting and you never know what will happen next. The realism and griminess of shootouts in the rain and show the character of the film. The scenes are filmed together collectively and not jump cut every second which let the seems flow and become drawn out. This allows it not to feel shaky and stitched together. The action allows more audience members to enjoy the movie even if not in tune with the intellectual concepts of the film. The last reason I believe Inception is one of the greatest movies of all time is because of the topic. The main plot-line of the movie involves dreams, an abstract idea, that becomes visualized in the film. Dreams are something that everyone can relate to. Dreams have been a controversial topic for many years. The ancient Egyptian Pharaohs believed they could predict the future and was a way to communicate with the Gods. We have learned much about the neural activity that actually control dreams in the twenty-first century, but dreams still have an unpredictable mystery that fascinates many with still more to be discovered about them. It shows the weirdness of dreams and give an explain of the psychology behind sharing dreams and the effects it can have. Some people argue against the genius of "Inception." A point made against it is: "How come when they went to Limbo, it was in DiCaprio's mind?" First of all, it is explained in the movie that if you create enough dream layers you will fall into "Limbo." They state in the dialogue of the movie when a character gets shot that if he dies, they are so heavily sedated that he won't wake up, he will fall into Limbo. However, when he falls into Limbo he will be exposed to whatever was created in the Limbo state by anyone else who has been there before in their shared dream. This is only DiCaprio's character because he went there with his wife when exploring the power of shared dreaming. This person simply was not paying attention to the film and did not understand what was going on. His incompetence shouldn't be costing this movie a bad rating.

10.title: Explore the subconscious within a dream... and within that dream dreaming.
10.content:
Let's create a multi-leveled dream where we can extract ideas off our enemies or implant an idea bypassing memories and consciousness: groundbreaking, original, complex, cerebral, psychological, systemic, and astute. The descriptors are insufficient to bring justice to this tremendously brilliant endeavor. The dialogue also presents obscure ideas that have rarely been explored in movies, or at least that I have not seen. At the onset the mystical dialogue attempts to explain the nature of the extraction, and, as the scenes take place, the viewer gets tempted by the explanation of worlds created by an architect where subjects can get robbed from their ideas or implanted in the case of the major heist of the movie.

Simply following and understanding the complex setting and the intricacies of the implanting is a challenge. The movie navigates a fast pace and is able to explain the complex events of the movie in a surprisingly effective style. Christopher Nolan presents the essential details in snippets of interactions that bring a lively and charismatic depiction to the process of learning about the heist. We also enjoy a diverse cast that amalgamates to deliver us an interesting exploration of Cobb's (Leonardo Dicaprio) perception. Ariadne (Ellen Page) is presented as a gifted college student that is extraordinarily apt at building mazes. She progressively gets to know more about the heist and Cobb's projections manifested in her mazes and, despite her repeatedly expressing her concern; we can't help but feel her emotions of compassion, sadness, and empathy. If Cobb was to show her the depths of his unconscious, the cast needed a sensitive rendition like the one displayed by Ariadne. Arthur is also, from the first scenes, supporting Cobb despite knowing all the baggage and the risks he implicates. Even despite Arthur risking everyone's life, the group still continues with the mission and finishes in dramatic fashion.

There are so many levels at which inception can be analyzed, but what is at the pinnacle of the experience for me is the innovation and dialogue. Movies as innovative and cerebral like inception should be celebrated and rewarded for their brilliant effort.

10.title: A Flawless Excecution, Showing the Power of Filmmaking
10.content:
Christopher Nolan makes some cinematic masterpieces, ones such as Memento (2000), I could rate up to even a 9 star review. However, Inception is truly beyond anything he has ever created.

After 9 consecutive viewings (over 3 days for a thesis paper), breaking down the film into many different film theories, it is clear that Nolan put an incredible amount of detail into this film in particular. Nolan's goal is clear, showing us throughout the film that the reality of life is irrelevant when compared to our perception of it (reality).

Throughout the film characters are subject to subconscious persuasion that ends up being more powerful than its counterpart conscious reality. Something such as an idea that is planted into the subconscious section of the mind completely alters the subjects reality. This is shown exceptionally well. The intended goal is to show the power of suggestion, and it comes off beautifully.

As a filmmaker, I know first hand the metaphor given through this film, the dream-space being the movie screen we show our "simulated realities" through. We have the power as filmmakers to make a false but believable reality, and it's our responsibility to change the world in a positive way. After watching this film, think about that. The filmmakers (Cobb and his team) are placing an idea in your mind (Fisher) without you even knowing it. As long as they don't break the suspension of disbelief, you're subject to whatever ideals they intend to execute.

This film, shows that flawlessly. Of all the countless times I've seen this film, not once have I been disappointed.

10.title: Wow
10.content:
Nolan, is a mind-bending masterpiece that seamlessly blends intricate storytelling with stunning visuals. The film explores the concept of dreams within dreams, challenging the audience to navigate a complex narrative. Leonardo DiCaprio delivers a compelling performance as Dom Cobb, a skilled extractor grappling with his own inner demons. The supporting cast, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Ellen Page, adds depth to the ensemble.

Nolan's direction is nothing short of brilliant, as he skillfully constructs a cinematic puzzle that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. The use of practical effects and minimal CGI enhances the immersive experience, making the dreamscapes feel tangible and surreal simultaneously. Hans Zimmer's iconic score intensifies the suspense, creating a sonic landscape that mirrors the film's psychological depth.

What elevates "Inception" beyond a typical blockbuster is its exploration of philosophical themes such as reality, memory, and the subconscious. The film invites contemplation on the nature of perception and the consequences of unchecked ambition. The intricacy of the plot demands the audience's full attention, rewarding those willing to engage with its intellectual challenges.

Despite its complexity, "Inception" maintains an emotional core, particularly in Cobb's relationship with his deceased wife, played poignantly by Marion Cotillard. This emotional undercurrent anchors the film, providing a relatable element amid the fantastical premise.

While some may find the layered narrative initially overwhelming, the meticulous craftsmanship and payoff in the final act justify the intellectual investment. "Inception" stands as a testament to Nolan's storytelling prowess, offering a cinematic experience that lingers in the mind long after the credits roll. In conclusion, "Inception" is a cinematic triumph that blends cerebral depth with thrilling action, solidifying its place as a modern classic in the science fiction genre.

10.title: INCEPTION Review - Buildings tilt. Streets coil. Characters float.
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" is one of the most best directed and looking movie you will ever watch. Are you awake? Or are you asleep? That is the question you will be asking yourself throughout the movie, and we will never truly know. Inception is a movie where buildings tilt. Streets coil. Characters float.

Leonardo DiCaprio conducts a team of high risk takers (or criminals depending on which way you look at it) who delve deep into a target's dreams, having numerous detours, good and bad. To get it out there straight away, the film itself is not for everyone, due to the high-complex storytelling that Nolan is presenting. Yes, this is one of those movies that will confuse you if you don't pay attention from start to finish.

The basic pot of"Inception" revolves around Dom Cobb (DiCaprio!) who is an expert at entering victims' dreams and "extracting" secrets through heir subconscious. Cobb cannot return home for certain reasons (Spoiler free review). He is approached by a powerful and wealthy businessman (Watanabe) who wants Cobb to "flip" his common pursuit and instead embed an idea in someone's mind.

Dom is required to enter the dreams of Fischer (Murphy) and persuade him to disassemble it to Watanabe's desire, with ultimately a return home. Cobb is joined by Arthur (Gordon-Levitt), Ariadne, an architect (Page) who constructs the dream worlds; Eames, a forger (Hardy) who can portray anyone at will; and a pharmacist (Rao) who enables very deep sleep.

The idea of Inception isn't as putting the victim to sleep for 10 hours. The team and their client not only enter the same dreams, but "enter dreams within his dreams and dreams, within those dreams". In other words, 10 hours turn into 10 years at the bottom level of the dream (limbo).

Christopher Nolan's "Inception"is a movie that won't disappoint any viewer, as long as they are prepared to sit down and watch this movie without any breaks or stops, as you will be immediately lost and / or confused about what is going on. My personal rating for this movie is a 9.9 / 10 and after watching this masterpiece, the high rating can easily be agreed with.

10.title: Absolutely Perfectly Brilliant!!!
10.content:
My goodness me is this a fantastically terrific movie!! I watched this movie in August and here I am now in November and I am still in awe of it! Christopher Nolan has delivered yet anther mesmerizing masterpiece and while I can write pages and pages of it, I realize this is a complex movie with many long reviews so I will try and keep this short...ish.

Inception tells the the story of Cobb (DiCaprio) who along with his team builds dreams. They then place their subject into that dream and allow them to "fill it with their secrets". That's about as simply as I can explain it because you can imagine that once that dream is filled, the manipulation Cobb can do is endless. Cobb gets enlisted to perform 'inception' on a high profile figure i.e: place an idea into the subject through placing them in a dream you created for them. The movie basically follows the protagonists in their mission all the while showing Cobb try to deal with the trauma in his life. That's all say about the storyline as I don't want to give too much away.

The positive points for this movie are endless. Firstly, the acting! Leonardo DiCaprio has matured into IMO the finest actor of his generation and his performance in Inception is truly outstanding, riveting, emotional, deep and definitely for me deserves the Best Actor Oscar! The rest of the cast pull in equally terrific performances which makes this one of the best acted films I have seen (and I have watched all the legends at their peak!). Secondly, the effects are jaw-dropping. Forget the Matrix "rip-offs" and what other nonsense the few negative reviews claim; the effects will leave you spellbound and completely make this movie a masterpiece. Thirdly, Hans Zimmer pulls in with a terrific score which captures the feel of the movie incredibly well and masterfully aids in building emotion where needed. Fourthly, the storyline is absolutely original and perfectly woven and told! Make no mistake, this is a complex movie with complex themes but with a fair bit of concentration, you will absolutely love it! I could go on and on...and so I shall; fifthly, the ending is utterly brilliant and will leave you reeling and thinking long after this movie ends (as it did with me!).

I have long waited for a movie of such high caliber and this blew my expectations right out the door and set new ones at a stratospheric level! If this movie does not get Best Picture, Best Screenplay, Best Director and Best Actor in the next Oscars, I will completely denounce the Oscars as a hoax! This movie is still playing in some theaters so I beg you, do yourself a favor and go see this; a movie which will definitely live to earn legendary status. All the hype is in fact underrated and you will not be disappointed no matter how high your expectations are! If there was a score of more than 10/10, I would give it. My only wish is that Nolan never stops making movies!

P.S. If you want to see a really good trailer of it, check out Inception Trailer 2 on youtube!

10.title: Okay But The Ending
10.content:
The beauty of the movie is that the audience is left with their own interpretations on the fate of the characters. Because the top continues to spin, one may assume he is still in the dream, which may lead them to find the astonishing ending as sad seeing that he is doomed in the dream space missing out on the lives of his children. One may view Leonardo being stuck in the dream as a happy ending because throughout the rest of the film he avoided his responsibilities to his family and job to find his deceased wife in dark areas of his mind. This perspective of ending would allow Dicaprio to be with not only his children, but his wife. I don't like most of that idea because he finally was able to let go of her and a happier version may be the other option the viewers may experience which is one in which he escaped the dream. The film comes to an end with the top spinning, however it does begin to wobble and may appear to some as beginning to fall. With this view, Leonardo has conquered his darkest fears and the crew accomplished their mission and can live his life free from worry with money and what was left of his family. However, with the knowledge that Christopher Nolan is quite a dark and mysterious man it is apparent that he wanted the audience to interact with the film and for them to decide whether they wanted the ending to be melancholiac or euphoric as a sort of emotional experiment. The audience was meant to be left not with the question of whether the top falls or not but how do their lives and depictions of the film change the fates and storyline of Inception. Inception itself is defined as a starting point, perhaps a starting point in knowing the furthest reaches of the human mind, not that of DiCaprio's character but of the audience members. The film is tragic and breathtaking and one must take it for what it is.

But the top does continue to spin.

10.title: Masterpiece
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" is a mind-bending masterpiece that defies the conventions of traditional storytelling. The film follows Dom Cobb, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, as he navigates the intricate world of corporate espionage through the manipulation of dreams. As Cobb and his team delve deeper into the subconscious, the lines between reality and illusion blur, leading to an exhilarating journey through the layers of the mind.

Nolan's direction is nothing short of visionary, seamlessly weaving together a complex narrative with stunning visual effects and a haunting score by Hans Zimmer. The film's concept of dream infiltration opens the door to a myriad of possibilities, allowing for breathtaking action sequences and mind-bending twists that keep audiences guessing until the very end.

DiCaprio delivers a captivating performance as Cobb, a troubled protagonist haunted by his past and driven by his desire to reunite with his family. His emotional journey serves as the heart of the film, grounding the fantastical elements in a deeply human story of redemption and forgiveness.

The supporting cast, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, and Tom Hardy, each bring their own unique talents to the table, adding depth and dimension to the ensemble. Their chemistry and camaraderie elevate the film beyond its high-concept premise, creating characters that are both relatable and compelling.

"Inception" is a cinematic experience unlike any other, challenging viewers to question the nature of reality and the power of the subconscious mind. It is a testament to Nolan's unparalleled skill as a filmmaker, pushing the boundaries of storytelling while delivering a thrilling and thought-provoking ride from start to finish. With its jaw-dropping visuals, innovative premise, and emotional depth, "Inception" stands as a modern classic that continues to captivate audiences years after its release.

10.title: #1 on my list
10.content: Christopher Nolan has written and directed a masterpiece for the ages. I have created my top ten best movies ever seen list and this is standing proudly at number one. I have heard the arguments against this film and they normally consist of viewers that were confused, couldn't get invested in the storyline and thought that the characters didn't get any backgrounds for us to get fully invested in them. Here is how I see it, and by no means do I condemn those that dislike this film. I tend to look at these characters as people involved in an Ocean's Eleven type plot. We don't get to know the background of everybody, but they all have specific talents that are needed for this job. Keep in mind that this movie is not really a character piece even though we do focus on Cobb for the entire film. In my personal professional opinion, the plot isn't confusing, just layered. For those that actually pay attention to the plot of a film, this movie has a very strong pot that is beautifully orchestrated throughout the 2h 30min run time. One only need to look and listen for what is going on. If you are one to fall asleep during a film longer than 2h then skip this until your wide awake. This movie does take a few watches to understand the gravity of everything going on and it only means your human if you finish the film and ask what the f**k just happened. The action is so well shot and is mind blowing to watch all the SFX. Now I wish to address the end all and be all of the reviews. The end shot of the movie. Many people have speculated as to how to decipher the end of this movie. I have heard the argument that it was all a dream. His kids were the same age so he must be in the dream world and not reality, and then there is the argument that I personally believe in and have the easiest time swallowing which is that he finished the job, got home and he is safe and sound in the real world. My answer may be completely wrong or I could be right on all cylinders. I honestly don't care what the real answer is because for all we know Chris Nolan made that ending intentionally to make us believe all these things and never agree on one answer. Whether or not there is a definite answer I am unclear about. Nolan loves secrets. The reason I find my answer easier to believe is because I have watched this movie four times (so far) and that seems to be the most logical answer and the one I am satisfied in believing. If somebody came up to me and said that I was wrong and they knew the real answer I wouldn't say prove it, I would say, OK, but this is what I believe. This movie is my favorite because I think about this movie every day of my life and recall that beautiful shot of the city folding and the hotel fight scene. All memorable. Now to end my review of this movie, I will address a question that everyone asks and nobody seems to know the answer to. People constantly ask why there is a snowy James Bond movie set in the climax scene. People say it is unnecessary and doesn't make sense. If you think back to when Ariadne was recruited, she was the brains behind designing the levels of the dream. So basically, using his creative mind and without telling us, Nolan wrote that Ariadne's character designed this level purely from her mind. He takes a liberty with this because it can by anything. We never hear or see Ariadne directly saying to the audience that the final battle will be in this setting, but she's just created it from her mind. Nothing is wrong with this, it just adds a grander and more dramatic scale. Maybe Nolan is a big Bond fan and wanted a set reminiscent of this. Nothing wrong with that. Nolan has crafted the most wholly original screenplay I have ever seen unfold onto the screen. While his ideas were influenced by other films the story itself and how it unfolds has never been done before. I doubt that I will encounter a movie better than this anytime soon, but it is possible. Until then I invite everyone to watch this film and bask in glory that is Inception.

10.title: A Nearly Perfect Movie – 10/10
10.content:
Okay, first of all, I had really high expectations for this film, I mean really high! And I didn't think that I was going to say this, but Inception actually exceeded my (super high) expectation. Christopher Nolan, now definitely one of my favorite directors, really did make a nearly perfect movie here.

Even though I have watched most of Nolan's films (Momento, Insomnia & Batman Begins), I only really started to notice his talent in The Prestige, which is also probably in my Top 10 movies of all time. Then of course, came The Dark Knight, which blew my mind and is my favorite movie of 2008.

But anyway, without talking too much s**t, my point is, is that he set the bar pretty high for himself.

Enter Inception A film about dreams! It is set in the near future where technology allows for people to invade another human's mind through his dreams. Now, Enter Leonardo DiCaprio, the best mind invader there is, has to get a team together to do his toughest job ever, inception, in other words, plant an idea inside a person's mind through his dreams. Blah blah blah, go watch the movie.

Even though the complexity of the story and the nearly two and a half hours of runtime, you don't need to worry about ever being bored or too confused. It keeps you intrigued the whole time, and although there might be some confusing parts, you never get to the point where you are completely lost in the complex storyline.

Apart from the highly intelligent story, there isn't much that is wrong with this movie. The cinematography, special effects and CGI is out of this world (literally) and it is like nothing you have ever seen before. The sound effects & musical score also fits in perfectly.

Inception also has a great cast. Most people will experience tragedy in their life, elation, triumph, and failure. Conveying these experiences into relatable emotions is a nearly impossible task. Watching the movie Inception will bring you into a sense of the only things that are of any 'REAL VALUE' in any (and everyone's) lifespan. Love, Integrity, Hope, Purpose, and Memory after we're gone.

Spoilers are not needed, but watching Inception more than once is likely required. It is a beautiful masterpiece showcased with breathtaking visuals, tear-jerking acting, and a meaningful plot that transcends religion as well as culture.

It is a beautiful movie beyond description that can only be cheapened by explanation. Never confuse the truly important moments in life as expendable. The most special moments are fleeting, and in reality, there is no device that can allow a person to get closure for things that we have allowed to pass us by.

10.title: A Near Perfect Film
10.content:
In this film, they advertise that Leonardo DiCaprio is in it, because he's a very famous actor. Across the top of the poster, it says his name. He is #1 at the top of the Top Billed Cast of 'Inception'. Now, if you look up Leonardo DiCaprio, his very top movie, at #1, of his Known For list, there is 'Inception'.

We have never seen anything like what is in this movie. It is a complicated, smart, action-packed drama/action film directed by Christopher Nolan, director of the 'Dark Knight' trilogy. I have no idea how the writers of this movie came up with such a masterpiece. The story of this is that DiCaprio's character, who is able to extract people's dreams, has a job that will get him from France (where he is now) to America, and back to kids, but he's not even sure this job is possible. It is to perform inception on a future owner of a very larger company.

When this movie starts out, you have no idea at all what is going on. You do eventually find out, though. I was extremely confused and was nearly doubting this film because I had no idea what was going on. When you do find out what was going on, your mind clicks into the movie. I thought that the film showed us what was going on at the perfect time. It didn't wait too long for us to loose interest, and it didn't happen too quick so that there was a boring part. Basically the whole movie was very interesting to me.

This film takes a challenge on itself to dig deeper and deeper to show us viewers everything about what's going on leading up to the huge, intense, action-packed sequence at the end of the movie. I shouldn't really say the end, because it starts a little earlier than I thought it would. That's one of the few problems in this movie. I thought the huge group of scenes started a little too early because I thought it could have taken more time to build it up. Anyway, it prevailed at the challenge it took, and there were many very cool things that happened. Scene by scene it takes us deeper into the planning of when they try inception. It gets very complicated there, but not really for us, like it was in the beginning. I meant it got complicating for the characters, kind of. They have to come up with a huge plan for the inception part of the movie, and you don't really have to completely invest your brain into it, because you're about to see it happen. Well, at least I didn't invest my brain into it.

The beginning was pretty action-packed, and the build-up was very interesting, but those parts of the movie are nothing compared to the last part of the movie. It's almost like they're sections: Section 1: Beginning; Section 2: Buildup; Section 3: Inception Part. The longest section was the Inception Part. I think it was about an hour and a half long, and for almost that last hour of the movie, I was at the edge of my seat. It was so intense, and I was going for the characters so much, I was basically talking to them, event though they couldn't hear. That's not weird, but seriously, I was saying, "NO! NO! Don't do it! Come on, come on!!!" There was so much action and there were many, many cool parts having to deal with the dreams. They were even cooler than the cool parts in the Buildup. By the end of the movie, you're so invested into the movie, you're not thinking about anything else. That section was so incredibly awesome to me. 'Inception' just truly amazed me. There was very good action and writing, the two things that prone to going bad the most in a movie.

So anyway, the ending was excellent, too, just like the rest of the movie. Especially the very last scene before the credits. It was just... Awesome. I really thought they couldn't have done that any better. I'll stop talking about it now. Well, I will buy 'Inception' on Blu-Ray. It is an overall excellent movie. It's two and a half hours long, but it justifies itself as a long movie. There were almost no boring parts in this movie. I actually think it would be worse if it wasn't this long. I strongly recommend this movie.

10.title: **Inception: A Mind-Bending Masterpiece**
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Inception" is a cinematic triumph that blends intricate storytelling with stunning visual effects. Released in 2010, this science fiction thriller takes audiences on a mesmerizing journey through the realms of dreams within dreams, challenging both the characters and the viewers to discern reality from illusion.

The film centers on Dom Cobb (Leonardo DiCaprio), a skilled thief who specializes in extracting secrets from deep within the subconscious during the dream state. Haunted by his past and unable to return home, Cobb is given a chance at redemption when a powerful businessman, Saito (Ken Watanabe), offers him a seemingly impossible task: to plant an idea in someone's mind, a process known as "inception."

Nolan's script is a masterclass in storytelling, weaving together multiple layers of dreams with precision and clarity. The narrative complexity is matched by the film's stunning visuals, from the zero-gravity fight scenes to the breathtaking folding cityscapes. Hans Zimmer's haunting score adds to the film's immersive experience, heightening the tension and emotional depth.

The ensemble cast delivers exceptional performances, with DiCaprio leading the charge as a man tormented by guilt and loss. Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, and Marion Cotillard also shine, each bringing depth to their multifaceted characters.

"Inception" is more than just a heist movie; it explores profound themes such as the nature of reality, the power of the subconscious, and the enduring impact of guilt and grief. Nolan invites the audience to question the very fabric of their own perceptions, leaving them pondering the film's ambiguous ending long after the credits roll.

Overall, "Inception" is a thought-provoking, visually spectacular film that cements Christopher Nolan's reputation as one of the most innovative directors of our time. It is a film that demands multiple viewings to fully appreciate its intricate layers and leaves an indelible mark on the landscape of modern cinema.

10.title: One of the best

The movie takes place on 4 scenes, the real world, and the 3 dream worlds. To identify which world is real, there is an object that's the key. Inception is a 2010 science fiction film written, co-produced, and directed by Christopher Nolan. The film stars a large ensemble cast that includes Leonardo DiCaprio, Ken Watanabe, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Marion Cotillard, Ellen Page, Tom Hardy, Dileep Rao, Cillian Murphy, Tom Berenger, and Michael Caine. DiCaprio plays Dom Cobb, a thief who commits corporate espionage by infiltrating the subconscious of his targets. He is offered a chance to regain his old life as payment for a task considered to be impossible: "inception", the implantation of another person's idea into a target's subconscious. Inception has received wide critical acclaim and numerous critics have praised its originality, cast, score, and visual effects. It won Academy Awards for Best Cinematography, Best Sound Editing, Best Sound Mixing, and Best Visual Effects, and was nominated for four more: Best Picture, Best Original Score, Best Art Direction, and Best Original Screenplay.

10.title: Masterful And Original

From the mind of Christopher Nolan comes this reality-bending sci-fi adventure that rivals The Matrix.

It is one thing to create an original idea. And another to develop that idea into a comprehensive story with depth and consistency. And still another to place a story arc within that world and have it be both engrossing and intelligent. Christopher Nolan---the writer and director---has done all of that.

Someone who has not seen the film can't fully appreciate the difficulty of making this script coherent. It would be wrong to explain here what was involved.

Besides the impressive world-crafting, the film offers a solid cast and high production values in every area. And the special effects live up to the high demands of the story.

Like most original works of curiosity, this film demands rewatching to fully appreciate its internal logic and the details of its crafting. I loved it after my first viewing, but now---after my third---I better understand it, allowing me to enjoy it on another level.
